<!-- LADDER-BOGUS-CLIMB-INTO-AIR-FIXED-2026-09-02 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ FIXED (NOT BENCH-VERIFIED): THE LADDER LOGIC PLANNED A STEP INTO THIN AIR (2026-09-02)

Found NOT by a live run, but by comparing `docs/BARITONE-PORT.md` (the special-terrain-rules
section, opened for the first time this session) against the current code — the same method that
closed the previous three sections of this audit. `FastPlanner.special()`, the ladder branch
(`FastPlanner.java:641-654`): continuing up/down a ladder column was offered as long as the target
cell simply FITS the body (`PlayerFit.bodyFits`), without checking that there is actually a rung or
a floor there — meaning a step into open air above the top rung or below the bottom one, exactly
the audit's own finding. Such a node could become the `best` node, whose chain gets returned as a
partial plan — a point in thin air.

FIXED (`a359fd38`): continuing along the column now requires the next cell to itself be a ladder;
landing FROM BELOW (`dy=-1`) additionally requires a real floor (`PlayerFit.supportTop` not NaN).
Exiting FROM ABOVE was already fixed separately (the side cardinal exit slightly further down in
the same file, with its own `supportTop` check) — not touched.

⛔ CAUGHT A SECOND, OWN MISTAKE BEFORE THE COMMIT: `cachedState` (inside `isLadder`) touches the
shared `scratch` (`BlockPos.Mutable`) ONLY on a cache miss — on a hit it leaves it wherever the
previous, unrelated call left it. The first draft called `PlayerFit.supportTop(world, scratch)`
right after `isLadder()` without an explicit `scratch.set(...)`, which on a cache hit would have
read the WRONG cell. Fixed with an explicit `scratch.set` before the call — the same pattern the
neighboring cardinal exit already uses a couple of lines below.

FIXED, NOT DEPLOYED AND NOT RE-MEASURED — the same reason as the `pathStatus` fix further up the
file (C8.1: `docker exec` blocked by the proxy, RCON unreachable, `gradlew`/`deploy_jar.sh` did
not run in this room). The change was read and logically justified, but NOT BENCH-VERIFIED — not
calling it done, calling it fixed-but-unverified (the checklist's Hard Ban).

NEXT STEP: once a bench is available — `nav_ladder` (or the closest course with a ladder) on a
paired measurement, watch whether the waypoint-in-air/partial plan disappears on ladder courses.

## ⭐⭐⭐ FOUND BY A LIVE RUN AND FIXED: `pathStatus` LIED ABOUT `arrived` (2026-09-01)

Found not by reading code, but by a REAL call over a workaround network path to the bench (see
C8.1 — `docker.sock` is still dead, but the MCP port `uctest-mc-tester1` is reachable directly at
`http://host.docker.internal:25350/mcp`). The first live measurement of the whole session.

REPRODUCED: `gotoXYZ(28,-60,0)` from position `(23.7,-60.0,0.7)` on a flat arena. The bot reached
`(27.0,-60.0,0.4)` and STOPPED FOREVER — `pathStatus()` held `arrived:false, distance:"1.5",
busy:true` UNCHANGED (same position to the hundredth) across 4 independent polls over ~15s, and
neither `stopPathing()` + a repeat `gotoXYZ` moved it a single centimeter. `getGameState()`
(another, independent method) confirmed the same position — not a single method's cache artifact.

CAUSE FOUND BY READING THE LOG, NOT BY GUESSING: `docker logs` (same workaround) showed
`FastNavigator: arrived (1.5)` — the engine CONSIDERS itself arrived at distance 1.5 and ITSELF
stops the `BlockPathWalker`. The bot hadn't frozen — it had FINISHED navigating correctly. The
bug is OUTSIDE, in the report: `FastNavigator.java:36,175` — `arrived = dist <= ARRIVE_DIST(=2.0)
&& goalRise<1.0`, while `Py4jEntryPoint.pathStatus():4373` (OLD code) — `out.put("arrived", dist <
1.5)` — a DIFFERENT, stricter and entirely unrelated threshold. A distance of 1.5 passes the
engine (`<=2.0`), but fails the status API (`<1.5` strictly). An agent running the `gotoXYZ →
pathStatus until arrived` loop (exactly the loop described in
`docs/features/AGENT_PY4J_LEVERS.md`) would hang FOREVER in this gap — not because the bot got
stuck, but because the API lied about its state. This is NOT the same mechanism as the
already-documented wandering stalls (`Nav.isPathing()` true with a motionless body, C10.1/top of
the file) — there NOTHING is actually moving the body; here the body has ALREADY arrived, the
report of it is just configured wrong.

FIXED (code changed, NOT deployed and NOT re-measured — deployment is unreachable via the same
path as before: `docker exec` blocked by the proxy, RCON unreachable, `gradlew`/`deploy_jar.sh`
did not run): `FastNavigator.ARRIVE_DIST` made `public` (was `private`), and
`Py4jEntryPoint.pathStatus()` now reads IT instead of holding a separate, independently-guessed
constant — rule 4c of this same checklist ("A duplicated constant will drift... Have one side
READ the other") applied, not ignored. `busy` (`hasActiveTask()` -> `isTungstenActive()` ->
`PATHFINDER.active`/`EXECUTOR.isRunning()`) was NOT touched — in my case navigation was going
through `BlockPathWalker`, not through `PATHFINDER`/`EXECUTOR`, and I did not trace `busy` to the
end; I don't want to blindly fix something I didn't fully understand.

⛔ ALONG THE WAY, NO EXTRA CHANGE NEEDED: `gotoFar` (`Py4jEntryPoint.java:4153`, javadoc "agent
loops: gotoFar → pathStatus (until arrived) → gotoFar") goes through the SAME `_gotoGoal`/
`pathStatus()` for every segment — the same bug COULD have hung a long distance on EVERY
intermediate leg too, not just a single-point `gotoXYZ`. The fix is shared, nothing separate to
fix, but it was worth explicitly checking rather than assuming by analogy — confirmed by reading,
`gotoFar` calls `gotoXYZ` internally (`:4172`), so it shares both the field and the method with it.

Also checked (not the same bug class, a separate, ALREADY-tracked finding): `;settings` live
showed the flag `arrivalAgreesWithTheSnap = false` — this is a DIFFERENT "arrival" mismatch
(snapping the goal to a suitable cell vs. an exact match), with its own mechanism-counter
`arrivedAtSnap` in `CustomBaritoneGoalTask.java:54-58`, not overlapping my fix at all. Not
touching it — already flagged and waiting for its own paired measurement.

NEXT STEP: rebuild and redeploy the jar once `gradlew`/`deploy_jar.sh` become available, and
confirm with a live run that `pathStatus` now correctly reports `arrived` at that same 1.5-2.0
distance. Until then the fix is READ and logically justified, but NOT BENCH-VERIFIED (the
checklist's Hard Ban: "Never call something done without a stand run" — not calling it done,
calling it fixed-but-unverified).

⛔⛔ FOUND AFTER THE FACT 2026-09-01, WHILE READING `docs/BARITONE-PORT.md`: this bug is NOT a
standalone finding, it is ONE OF SIX+ already-documented cases of exactly this defect class. The
"GOALS AND ARRIVAL" section of that file (produced 2026-07-30, five weeks before my live
measurement) states VERBATIM: "tungsten... re-invents "arrived" five more times with five
different radii and dimensionalities across FastNavigator, BlockPathWalker, GotoCommand and
PathExecutor" (finding #331: "Arrival is defined five times with different radii and
dimensionality, none of them the planner's own in-goal test"). My `Py4jEntryPoint.pathStatus` is
the SIXTH definition, that same audit simply didn't count it (the py4j layer wasn't among the 8
areas it broke the analysis into). The ROOT CAUSE, which that audit calls the CORRECT FIX rather
than a patch on a patch: baritone has ONE `Goal` object (`isInGoal` + `heuristic` together,
`Goal.java:38,48,68`), used EVERYWHERE — by the search to stop, by the result classifier, and by
the behavior that announces arrival. tungsten has no goal abstraction at all — a bare `BlockPos`
and scattered, independently-guessed "have we arrived" checks. My fix made ONE pair
(`pathStatus` + `FastNavigator`) consistent, it did not build the `Goal` abstraction — meaning ONE
rattle out of at least six was cleaned up, not the root as a whole. The section in full (13
findings, `docs/BARITONE-PORT.md` around line ~293) is a ready-made, already-written plan for a
full CORE FIX, if someone takes this work on as a focus; not fixing the other five separately —
it's a large, coherent task that needs an overall `Goal` design, not five independent one-off
patches.

<!-- ATTACK-KEY-THEFT-FOUND-2026-08-31 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ FOUND AND NAMED: THE MOB-DEFENSE CHAIN STEALS THE ATTACK KEY FROM THE MINER (2026-08-31)

LINE `MobDefenseChain:645`:

```java
if (fireBlock != null) { putOutFire(...); wasPuttingOutFire = true; }
else {
    // Stop putting stuff out if we no longer need to put out a fire.
    mod.getInputControls().release(Input.CLICK_LEFT);
    wasPuttingOutFire = false;
}
```

The comment says "if we no longer NEED to". `wasPuttingOutFire` is set two lines above and is
NEVER READ, so the release fires on EVERY tick when the bot isn't standing in fire — meaning
almost always. And the attack key is what tungsten digs WITH: it aims, presses, and vanilla breaks
whatever's under the crosshair.

THE CHAIN, EACH LINK ITS OWN MEASUREMENT:

```
the miner IS RUNNING          stallMiner 1143/6, 2260/6, 877/1   (99.5%)
aim IS ON PLAN                 899 of 903 ticks in one run
the key IS PRESSED             breakAim aimed 803, 1905, 899, 734
FOREIGN CODE RELEASES IT       attackThief=[MobDefenseChain:645 x299]
vanilla almost never breaks    mine = 135/4180 = 3.1% during the playthrough
                                against 73% on nav_break, where this chain is idle
```

VERIFICATION OF THE FIX, FIRST ARM (`fireReleaseNeedsFire` flag):

```
             BEFORE                          AFTER
attackThief  MobDefenseChain:645 x299        (none)
mine         135/4180 = 3.1%                 51/1 = 98%
mechanism    —                               fireReleaseSkipped=12227
```

THE MECHANISM AND THE INTERMEDIATE METRIC MOVED TOGETHER — exactly what the "break whatever's in
the way" fix was missing, where the counter fired hardest in the single pair that went AGAINST the
fix.

⛔ WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED: THE OUTCOME. Idle time and rungs per pair have NOT been captured —
aggregates kept dying with the session. Three fixes in this line already had a fully working
mechanism and ZERO shift in the outcome (wander target 94%->0%, idle lock 45-55%->10%, "break
what's in the way" 137 triggers). So the flag STAYS OFF pending a paired idle-time measurement
(rule 4a2).

⛔ A BENCH TRAP THAT FIRED TWICE THIS SESSION: an aggregate with `--pin-alt` killed halfway through
LEAVES the pin set in the bench's `tungsten.json`. Both times the bench was left with
`fireReleaseNeedsFire=True`, and any following run would have executed the changed arm while being
logged as a control. CHECK THE BENCH'S FLAGS BEFORE EVERY RUN, not after.

## ⛔ THE "BREAK WHAT'S IN THE WAY" FIX — THE WIN IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE COUNTER PROVES IT (2026-08-31)

A clean pair by rule 4a1: the mechanism is non-zero in EVERY arm with the fix (137, 3, 2) and ZERO
in every control, arms alternate B/A/B/A/B/A per rule 4r.

```
seed               rungs   idle change / control     overlaps in the changed arm
-308 150 -1439      5 /4    177s (30%)    65s (11%)              137
-8   150 -1439      4 /2     67s (11%)   265s (45%)                3
1192 150 -1439      1 /3     66s (11%)   476s (82%)                2

idle     -165.3 s/run     t -1.09  NOT ESTABLISHED  [+112, -198, -410]
share    -28.4%/run       t -1.09  NOT ESTABLISHED
rungs    +0.33/run        t +0.28  NOT ESTABLISHED
```

⛔ THE KEY POINT: THE DIRECTION OF THE MECHANISM CONTRADICTS THE DIRECTION OF THE OUTCOME. The
pair where the fix FIRED 137 times produced +112s AGAINST the fix. The pairs where it fired 3 and
2 times — i.e. barely fired at all — produced the entire win (-198 and -410s). The fix CANNOT be
having its largest effect in the runs where it almost never executed, so -165s/run is inter-run
variance, not the fix's effect.

WITHOUT THE MECHANISM COUNTER THIS WOULD HAVE BEEN A HEADLINE: "-165s idle per run, -28% share".
This is EXACTLY what rule 4a1 exists for, and here it fired not on an empty pair, but on a pair
that LOOKED informative.

THE `mineTheBlockInTheWay` FLAG STAYS OFF. The code and counters stay: the diagnosis behind them is
established (0 of 8016, 0 of 3548); the ONLY thing not established is that this fix cures the idle
time.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE REGARDLESS OF THE VERDICT: the chain was measured link by link — a stalled dig
doesn't break anything (0 of 8016), a converged aim lands on a different cell (46-90% misses), a

<!-- WANDER-TARGET-DOES-NOT-EXIST-2026-08-29 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ THE WANDER TARGET DOESN'T EXIST IN 94% OF CASES — BUT THAT DOESN'T EXPLAIN THE SYMPTOM (2026-08-29)

Counter `wanderTung=<picked>/<driven>/u<no-stand>`, three runs:

```
94/13/u85     164/28/u158     9/9/u9        ->  252 of 267 = 94%
```

THE MECHANISM. `TimeoutWanderTask` builds the target as `(anchor.x + cos*r, ANCHOR.Y, anchor.z +
sin*r)` with r up to 120 blocks. XZ spirals out over the real terrain, Y never moves — the point
is almost always inside rock or in mid-air. And this isn't just a wasted pick: a new target can
ONLY be taken when `!TungstenHelper.isActive()`, and the search for an unreachable point holds this
flag true. Hence thousands of ticks of wandering, half a block of covered distance, and the
progress-check reset being denied on 83-94% of ticks.

A CORE FIX (flag `wanderTargetFollowsTheGround`, OFF BY DEFAULT): search for support within a band
around the requested height (48 down, 24 up) and LEAVE the point as-is if there's no support — by
construction it cannot get worse. It searches from the REQUESTED height, not from the world
surface: a mountain top 120 blocks away isn't what wandering was actually aiming for.

THE MECHANISM FIRED COMPLETELY:

```
control      u23/23 (100%)   u606/619 (98%)   u50/52 (96%)
with the fix u0/316  (0%)    u2/70     (3%)
```

⛔ BUT THE OUTCOME IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THIS WEAKENS THE CAUSAL LINK. Idle time +10.5 s/run
over 2 pairs (t +0.19), one pair against. And MOST IMPORTANTLY: in these same runs dead time
STILL sits in wandering (56%), in both arms. Meaning the target is fixed and the symptom is
unchanged — so the non-existent target was NOT (the sole) cause of the idle time, however
convincing 94% looks. Recording this here so the next pass doesn't mistake the mechanism for the
outcome.

Few pairs (one lost: client at 7 fps, the bench rejected it itself). Still accumulating.
Separately: the counter used to print only inside `wanderTung=.../uN`, and `paired_ab` read
`mech=?/?` — there is now a dedicated token `wanderTargetUnstandable=<n>` (the repository already
had a commit specifically about this lesson).

The phenomenon DOES exist, but it's two to three orders of magnitude smaller than the broken
counter showed. A hundred stolen presses over ~12000 ticks of a run cannot explain a 30% idle
rate. As a CAUSE of dead time the hypothesis is rejected; as a minor defect it remains, not a

<!-- WANDER-PATHS-AND-DOES-NOT-MOVE-2026-08-29 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ INSIDE WANDERING: NAVIGATION "IS DRIVING A ROUTE", BUT THE BODY STANDS STILL (2026-08-29)

The wander counters were read BY THEIR DEFINITIONS, not by their names (I first read them wrong,
and that matters): `wanderMoved` is CENTIMETERS covered on this task's ticks, while `wanderDenied`
= `wanderResetDenied` — progress-check resets that were DENIED because the body hadn't moved for
40+ ticks WHILE `Nav.isPathing()` is TRUE.

```
run    wander   covered   resets denied   targets picked/driven
  1      5414     52 cm       5086 (94%)         12/12
  2      4662    173 cm       4327 (93%)        124/18
  3      4487     17 cm       3730 (83%)        192/24
  4      1872      0 cm       1716 (92%)         76/9
  5      4174   1321 cm       2720 (65%)        110/27
  6       134     76 cm          0                0/0
```

READS AS FOLLOWS: wandering holds the tick for thousands of cycles, covers HALF A BLOCK per run
(ZERO in run four), and on 83-94% of those ticks navigation CLAIMS it's driving a route, with a
motionless body. This is not "wandering fails to pick a target": targets ARE picked (12-192 per
run) and handed to the drive.

THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT CLASS FROM EVERYTHING ELSE THIS SESSION. Everything above is about the
QUALITY OF THE GUIDE (where the route leads). Here the route is beside the point: the navigation
layer reports "driving", while the body doesn't move. The next pass's question is whether the
drive gets the body moving AT ALL, and exactly what makes `Nav.isPathing()` return true across
these thousands of ticks.

WHAT IS NOT BEING CLAIMED: that wandering is at fault. It is a RECOVERY mechanism and kicks in
when everything else has given up — "where the time sits" and "who's to blame" remain separate
claims. What's established is that dead time SITS here, and that within it navigation lies about

<!-- DIST-FROM-START-IS-NOT-A-DISTANCE-2026-08-29 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ ROOT CAUSE: THE "DISTANCE FROM START" IN THE COARSE SEARCH IS NOT A DISTANCE (2026-08-29)

Both puzzles — why routes-to-nowhere come out AND why `bsStub` reads zero — are explained by ONE
function.

```java
private static double getDistFromStartSq(BlockNode n, Vec3d start) {
    boolean fix = TungstenConfig.get().smartMoves;      // FALSE on the bench
    double xDiff = start.x - n.getPos().x;
    double yDiff = (fix ? start.y : start.x) - n.getPos().y;   // start.X minus node.Y
    double zDiff = (fix ? start.z : start.x) - n.getPos().z;   // start.X minus node.Z
    return xDiff*xDiff + yDiff*yDiff + zDiff*zDiff;
}
```

The typo is known and DELIBERATELY left behind a flag ("correcting it alone regresses the
blind-scan search"). But `smartMoves` is off on the bench, meaning this exact typo is what's live.

FIRST CONSEQUENCE — A GATE THAT'S ALWAYS OPEN. `bestSoFar` is supposed to hand back a path only
when progress exceeds MIN_DIST_PATH (in this class = 5). That's the value it compares against.
For a bot at x=1792, the term `start.x - n.y` is on the order of 1700, its square is in the
millions: the gate passes ALWAYS, regardless of real progress. This is how a "partial path"
leading nowhere reaches the physical leg. The guarantee in the exhaustion-exit's comment
("bestSoFar only returns a path when there's real forward progress") IS NOT MET.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE — A COUNTER THAT CANNOT FIRE. `salvage()`'s first line takes `movedSq` from
this same function and takes an early exit when `movedSq > MIN_DIST_PATH*MIN_DIST_PATH`. The
number is huge, the exit always fires, `bsStub++` is UNREACHABLE. Hence `bsStub=0/0` in every run
— and hence the mistaken conclusion of the 2026-08-28 entry that there are no stub guides.

WHAT MEASURED THIS (3 runs, a counter by exit type):

```
run1  coarseNowhereBy[stalledx11]   of 11
run2  coarseNowhereBy[stalledx20]   of 20
run3  coarseNowhereBy[stalledx17]   of 17
```

48 of 48 — the `stalled` exit, zero through `exhaustedPartial`. This DISPROVED my own guess that
`bsStub` is blind because of a `salvage()` bypass: `stalled` goes THROUGH salvage. It's blind
because of the arithmetic inside it, not because of the execution path.

A COORDINATE DEPENDENCY THIS PREDICTS AND THAT NEEDS CHECKING: the distortion grows with
|start.x|. The aggregate ran at x = -8, 892, 1192, 1792 — all far from zero. Near spawn the
coordinates are small, and the defect should be weaker there. This is a testable prediction, not
a post-hoc explanation.

NOT FIXING THIS BLINDLY. The comment claims a standalone fix breaks the blind scan (course A
lives on these junk partial paths). A lever already exists — `smartMoves`, which enables both the
correct formula and the other `bestSoFar` branch. Next pass: a paired A/B with `smartMoves=true`,
judged by IDLE TIME, with `bsStub` as the mechanism counter (it must read 0 in the control by
construction, and must come alive in the arm with the fix — that itself verifies the formula
actually changed).

<!-- GUIDE-STUB-SPLIT-2026-08-29 -->
## ⛔ THE GUIDE STUB IS TWO DIFFERENT DEFECTS, AND ONE MEASUREMENT MISTAKE OF MY OWN (2026-08-29)

The `guideSrc` counter was added, run, and REDONE, because the first version measured the wrong
thing.

A MISTAKE IN MY OWN COUNTER. The first version only asked about the guide's length (threshold
1.8) and did NOT ask how far the target was. A half-block guide to a target half a block away is a
correct plan, not a stub, and there are many of those in the stall profile. The "coarse 91-99% to
nowhere" numbers from the first pass are INFLATED and unfit for any conclusion. This is exactly the
mistake I criticized `fast.path.size() >= 2` for two hours earlier: measuring the guide without
asking where it was supposed to lead.

AND THE TRAP I FELL INTO: `MIN_DIST_PATH` IS TWO DIFFERENT CONSTANTS WITH THE SAME NAME.
`PathFinder.MIN_DIST_PATH = 1.8`, `BlockSpacePathFinder.MIN_DIST_PATH = 5`. The `bestSoFar` gate
uses the five, my counter measured against 1.8. When referencing this name, ALWAYS name the class.

THE `truncateAtBreaks` HYPOTHESIS WAS STATED BEFORE MEASUREMENT AND REFUTED IN THIS FORM. It
claimed: the `subList(0, max(i,1))` cut at the very first step requiring digging leaves ONE node,
and this explains everything. A run with `trunc=1/0` and 32 routes-to-nowhere killed it in its
general form.

WHAT THE NUMBERS SAY AFTER FIXING THE COUNTER (3 runs):

```
        fast total/to_nowhere   coarse total/to_nowhere   cuts/down_to_one_node
run1          25/8                  43/25                   15/4
run2         155/121                96/71                  146/120
run3          34/28                 53/49                   31/27
```

THE DEFECT SPLITS IN TWO:

1. For FAST, "to nowhere" is almost exactly equal to the number of cuts down to one node: 120
   against 121 and 27 against 28. In run1 — 4 against 8, half. So the match holds in two runs out
   of three: A STRONG HYPOTHESIS, BUT NOT ESTABLISHED. The mechanism is plausible and named: a
   route whose first step requires digging or bridging is returned as a single start cell instead
   of "a dig plan plus a guide that actually has somewhere to go".
2. For COARSE (71, 49, 25 to nowhere) the cut explains NOTHING, and `bsStub` reads zero in every
   run. This is a separate, not-yet-named cause.

NEXT MEASUREMENT: split `guideFromCoarseNowhere` BY the coarse search's exit type. The exhaustion
exit (`partial` from `bestSoFar`) returns BYPASSING `salvage()` — and `bsStub++` lives inside
`salvage()`. A zero counter here means "my exit stays silent", and that is literally the case.

<!-- GUIDE-IS-A-STUB-2026-08-28 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ WHY THE DRIVE DOESN'T FINISH THE JOB: THE GUIDE LEADS FROM A CELL BACK INTO ITSELF (2026-08-28)

Measured from the logs of the two aggregates above (12 runs), without a single new run — the data
was already collected, nobody had tried reading it. 78 `guide halts` lines, 69 distinct
situations:

```
guide shorter than 2 BLOCKS (leads to nowhere)   59/69
of those, two nodes in the SAME cell               58
uncompleted step                          hop[0,0,0] — from a cell back into itself
target at that moment                     median 32 blocks
```

The ten cases where the guide is real give 3.9 blocks toward a target 3.3 blocks away. Meaning
ONLY short, local routes get built, and everywhere else the physical leg gets a route that says
"go to where you're already standing", honestly never finds arrival, and stops.

THIS EXPLAINS THE ENTRY ABOVE. The snap-arrival fix repairs the route's last step, which never
happens: `snap=6484/5188/1296` with `arrivedAtSnap=0` — five thousand shifted targets and not a
single case of the bot standing in the chosen cell.

TWO CIRCUMSTANCES THAT MADE THIS TAKE SO LONG TO FIND:

1. THE COUNTER WAS ALREADY SAYING THIS, AND NOBODY READ IT. `gvpTinyGuide` prints in the verdict
   line of every run: `gvp=70/tiny68`, `44/tiny43`, `15/tiny15`. The share of "tiny" guides is
   overwhelming in ALL twelve runs.
2. `bsStub` READS ZERO IN ALL TWELVE. The 2026-08-28 entry ("the mechanism doesn't fire, the flag
   stays off") concluded from this zero that there are no stub guides. There ARE stub guides —
   they come from an exit OTHER than the one `bsStub` is attached to. A zero counter means "my
   exit stays silent", not "the phenomenon doesn't exist", and that cost a whole pass to learn.

There are EXACTLY TWO guide producers: `FastPlanner` (accepted via `fast.path.size() >= 2` — a
check IN NODES, exactly the mistake `salvage()` already has a comment about, "a stub is measured
in blocks") and `BlockSpacePathFinder.search`. A `guideSrc=<fast>/<fastToNowhere>/<coarse>/
<coarseToNowhere>` counter has been added — it counts IN BLOCKS, against MIN_DIST_PATH, pure
diagnostics with no behavior change. It will name the culprit.

extreme case is a run with `snap=6484/5188/1296` and `arrivedAtSnap=0`: five thousand shifted
targets, meaning five thousand arrival checks that are unsatisfiable by construction, and NOT ONE
case of the bot ending up in the cell the drive was leading it to. So an unsatisfiable check isn't
what's holding the bot: it simply NEVER REACHES the shifted cell. The fix repairs the route's last
step, which never happens.

THE NEXT MEASUREMENT FROM HERE: not "more pairs for this flag", but why the drive doesn't get the
bot into the cell it chose itself. Measure the distance from the bot to `snappedGoalCell` at the
moment the task gives up or re-requests the approach.

windows, 0/13, 4/10. The only shuttling run with the fix comes from an EMPTY pair (mechanism 0),
and in the informative pair it was the CONTROL that shuttled (4/22 against 0/13). Shuttling in
this aggregate appears in both arms and says nothing about the flag.

STAYS IN THE CODE: the `arrivedAtSnap` counter (it's what separated the informative pairs from the
empty ones) and the flag itself, off, pending a measurement where the mechanism fires in more than
a quarter of runs.

<!-- ARRIVAL-VS-SNAP-2026-08-28 -->
## ⭐⭐⭐ PROFILE A NAMED IN FULL: THE DRIVE AND THE ARRIVAL CHECK ARE AIMING AT DIFFERENT CELLS (2026-08-28)

The counter TODOS has been asking for since 2026-08-26 ("a counter on the target source first")
has been added, and it names the source in one line:

```
snap=200/197/3/self134[GetToBlockTaskx134]
atGoal=10(ex10,ytol0)@GetToBlockTask@block(-311,125,-257)x10
```

One task, ONE block, ten consecutive plans into a cell the bot is already standing in. All the
matches are EXACT — meaning the layers agree on WHERE the bot is, and disagree on WHERE it was
sent.

THE MECHANISM (structural, not a bug in either half): `driveTungstenPrimary` aims at
`snapGoalToStandable(goal)`, and the snap only moves the target if it's UNSTANDABLE — here, 197 of
200 requests. `isFinished()`, meanwhile, asks `AltoGoal.Block.reached`, which needs the REQUESTED
cell to be OCCUPIED. So for every shifted target, the arrival check is UNSATISFIABLE BY
CONSTRUCTION: the drive puts the bot next to a log, the task says "not there" and asks again every
tick. `snapToSelf` only counts ticks where `isFinished()` has ALREADY returned false (its gate
sits above the snap) — meaning these 134 are 134 unsatisfiable checks, not "almost arrived".

THE FIX (flag `arrivalAgreesWithTheSnap`, OFF BY DEFAULT): remember the cell the snap chose, and
consider the task finished once the bot is standing in it. Recomputed every tick (the snap depends
on the world and the bot's position). Can only ADD completions that would otherwise be impossible:
you cannot stand in an unstandable cell, so the exact check there would never have passed anyway.

A RISK recorded BEFORE the measurement: a caller that specifically needs the exact cell occupied,
or one that re-requests the approach the moment it's out of reach, would turn a stall into
SHUTTLING. Measure both idle time AND shuttling (`shuttle.py`). The mechanism counter is
`arrivedAtSnap`.

## ⭐⭐ FOUND: THE COARSE SEARCH'S TIMEOUT EXIT HANDS BACK A STUB (2026-08-28)

Three stall dumps from one aggregate, to be read only together (rule five):

```
run1  bsEnd[c24 t0   s1  x0] closest0.96m  guide=n11   the coarse search is healthy
run3  bsEnd[c63 t0   s0  x0] closest0.50m  guide=n2    healthy, target one step away
run2  bsEnd[c0  t105 s11 x0] closest18.05m guide=n2    NOT ONE search reached the target
```

Run2's profile: 117 coarse searches, not one reached the target, 1.48M nodes expanded, and the
guide handed to the physical leg is TWO nodes, ending 29.8 blocks from the target. A small failure
budget — 1920ms, and `failing` doesn't clear until some node has moved MIN_DIST_PATH away from the
start — meaning more than three minutes of a ten-minute run went into computing a route that
leads nowhere, with `wander=137 wanderMoved=0`.

WHY A STUB. The timeout exit hands back `bestSoFar()` — a MONOTONIC record of heuristic
improvement. If no descendant ever beat the seed, the record stays on the start node, and the
caller gets the start plus one move — that isn't a route. The EXHAUSTION exit has had a fallback
since #67 ("the closest cell reached"), while the TIMEOUT exit — the very one this run hits — had
nothing.

AND THIS FALLBACK HAS NEVER WORKED, NOT ONCE. `closestToGoal` is declared above the loop,
commented, read further down — and NEVER ASSIGNED ANYWHERE. Always null, the branch is
unreachable. A disconnected EXECUTOR — the mirror image of rule one.

THE FIX (FLAG `coarseFallsBackToClosestCell`, OFF BY DEFAULT, NOT MEASURED): assign
`closestToGoal` when popping from the heap, and serve BOTH exits with one `salvage()`. The
counters are written independently of the flag, so the control arm will say for itself how much
material the fix has to work with:

```
bsStub=<stubs>/<of them had something closer>@<farthest such>cm/used<n>
```

`used` is the mechanism counter: 0 in the control and non-zero in the arm with the fix, otherwise
the pair measured nothing (rule 4a1). GATE: a paired `gamer_smoke --pin-alt` judged by IDLE TIME,
not by rungs (rule 4a2).

IMPORTANT: the timeout regime is NOT universal — two dumps out of three show a healthy coarse
search. This is one of three stall profiles, not the sole cause.

## ⭐ SEARCH STARVATION REMOVED: THE STALL DETECTOR WAS KILLING IT ITSELF (2026-08-25)

Course 1219. A chain of measurements, each step backed by a number:

   `dy01=-3.1`.
2. The fall guard, which is supposed to reject such a move, is NOT CALLED: `fallChk 0/0`.
   `getChildren` has two exits, and the "smart" one leaves via an early `return` BEFORE the
   filter -- `SmartMoves` allows itself a descent of up to three blocks (`MAX_DESCEND=3`)
   past the common gate. Folded both exits into one gate, but it CANNOT BE CREDITED: on this
   course it didn't fire (`smart 0-0`).
3. The real trail: `searchAborted=28` while `tryEmit=0` -- the physics leg gets killed BEFORE
   the first attempt to hand off a route. Two fixes at GUESSED spots (resume in PathExecutor)
   didn't fire once (`resumeKept0`). The third fix in a row that didn't fire -- stopped
   guessing.
4. Tagged EVERY `stop.set(true)`. First pass -- `stopBy: none`: only tagged tungsten, while

   ```

   CustomBaritoneGoalTask@521 :  7   (gives up "goal unreachable" after 14,000 ms)
                         total 28  =  searchAborted=28
   ```

The loop closed on its own: the bot is walled in (`head:dirt`, `mine:Y`) and not moving ->
after 5 s the detector -> kills the search -> the search doesn't make it to a first output ->
no route -> no movement. New captures never come -> nobody resets it. Till the run ends.

FIX (`stallResetSparesAVirginSearch`): don't raise the threshold (that's a hardcode), instead
forbid tearing down a search that HASN'T PRODUCED ANYTHING YET -- such a search isn't a "bad
route", it's unfinished, and killing it can't help. Termination is still bounded by the
search's own budget.

the bot is `BlockPathWalker` with its own BFS. Every pass in this series (the 3-block descent,
the common gate, the resume guard) was done in layers that DON'T EXECUTE here -- hence three

METHODICAL CONCLUSION (more valuable than the finding itself): before fixing a layer, prove
it EXECUTES. A counter at the function's entry costs one measurement and removes a whole
series of empty fixes. This session's cost of the mistake: four passes.

`FastPlanner.plan` is plain A*, where `best = startNode`. If not a single successor is

the queue receives a collapsed route (`mqRefused(short=1229)` with `tickBfs=1229`).

CONCLUSION: the STARTING CELL is being rejected -- from the point where the bot stands, not
a single successor is generated, in half the cases. This is the mechanism behind "a thousand
steps with no closing of distance".

  ladder ceiling -> APPROACH failure (targets 8/0, gives up at 14.2 blocks)
  -> queue: 600 starts, 1000 steps, 0 closing
  -> route collapses: 100% of BFS ticks against 70% in the healthy run
  -> source: `FastPlanner.plan` returns <2 cells
  -> cause: 53 of 105 plans expand NOT A SINGLE node from the start

and `PlayerFit` for the cell the bot is standing in (standing in water/on an edge/inside a

## ⛔ THE "TRUST PHYSICS AT THE START" FIX -- MEASURED AND REJECTED (2026-08-26)

Hypothesis: `FastPlanner` refuses to plan from the cell the bot is STANDING IN
(`supportTop = NaN` -> `continue` -> zero successors -> a one-cell route). The basis was
strong: `plan=95/8448/253ms/sz39/zero57(e0=0,e1=57)` -- the budget never fired even once, and
57 of 95 plans died with a childless start node.

```
BASE  (flag off)   nav 14/14   craft 22/22
FIX   (flag on)    nav 13/14   nav_water FAIL
```

Rejected, and the premise was wrong: `supportTop = NaN` does NOT mean "the world got it
wrong". It means "the bot is NOT STANDING" -- it's airborne, falling, or SWIMMING. Feeding in
a fake ground support forces a ground route to be built from there.

Moving the rescue past the water/ladder branch didn't help -- `nav_water` failed again,
because the rescue also fires on floating starts that `isWater()` doesn't count as water. Two
independent confirmations.

RETRACTED SEPARATELY: the bot falling out of the world on `nav_gaps` ("min Y -149.6 with a
floor at -60") -- I initially attributed it to this fix. WRONG -- it reproduces with the flag
OFF too, and the suite itself re-measures it on fresh clients and calls it bench wear. The
only real regression was `nav_water`.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND VALUABLE -- THE CORRECTED READING OF `e1=57/95`:
it's not "the planner wrongly rejects the start", it's **60% OF PLANS ARE REQUESTED WHILE THE
BOT HAS NO SUPPORT** -- and they correctly fail. What needs fixing is not the support, it's
the moment of the request: either allow a start in the cell the bot WILL LAND ON
(`BlockSpacePathFinder.resolveStart` already does exactly that), or don't issue a plan until
it has landed.

NEXT PASS: move `resolveStart`'s logic into `FastPlanner` (start = the landing cell) and
measure `e1` before/after. Same-root fix, but without the false premise.

WHY IT DOESN'T FIRE (a hypothesis for the next measurement, NOT a conclusion): `FastNavigator`

## ⭐ ALL THE SLOT CLICKS ARE ONE INVENTORY SWEEP (2026-08-26)

Attribution started working after tightening the sample rate (1/64 instead of 1/1024 -- on
a healthy run 1/1024 gave three samples, nothing to rank):

```
shRefresh=21/0      21 passes, 0 of them started with a BUSY cursor
shIssued=1512       21 x 72 = 1512   EXACT match
shWho=[PlayerInteractionFixChain:106 x23]     100% of samples
```

Mechanism: `PlayerInteractionFixChain` calls `SlotHandler.refreshInventory()` once every
30 s, which walks 36 slots and does TWO clicks per slot (pick up/put down) -- 72 clicks in
one tick, THROUGH `clickSlotForce`, i.e. BYPASSING the rate limiter. The only guard: "are we
breaking a block".

NOT SHIPPING A FIX, AND THIS IS THE MAIN POINT: I was going to forbid the sweep when the
cursor is busy (that would explain `mv` 2255 pickups against 3 placements). But
`withCursor=0` -- in healthy runs it NEVER starts with a busy cursor, so the guard would be
an EMPTY SHELL. This is the fifth case this session where measuring the input saved a
non-executing fix from being shipped.

WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED: the stalled run gave `shIssued=603671`. At 72 clicks per pass
that's 8384 sweeps in ten minutes, i.e. 14 per second against a 30-second timer. Either the
timer is being reset somewhere else, or the sweep is being called from somewhere else too.
The instrument (`shRefresh`, `shWho`) will now name it on the very next recurrence.

## ⛔ THE TIMER HYPOTHESIS IS DROPPED BY READING, NOT BY MEASUREMENT (2026-08-26)

The theory was elegant: the `TimerGame` clock is CONNECTION TICKS (`getTicks()/20.0`), on a
reconnect the counter resets, the timer becomes permanently triggered, the inventory sweep
runs EVERY tick -- 72 clicks x 20/s = 1440 per second, i.e. ~864,000 over ten minutes, which
matches the observed 603,671 by order of magnitude.

READING THE BASE TIMER KILLS IT:

```java
getDuration() { return currentTime() - prevTime; }
elapsed()     { return getDuration() > interval; }
```

A BACKWARD jump in the clock gives a NEGATIVE difference, meaning the timer stops firing
entirely -- the opposite of what's observed. And `reset()` sits right after the sweep, so
this branch physically cannot produce more than one pass per 30 s.

CONCLUSION: the 603,671 clicks don't come from here. Other places remain that bypass the
rate limiter -- `clickSlotForce` in `forceEquipItem` (SlotHandler:341,401,406,413,418). In
healthy runs equipping is rare, which is why the sample showed 100% sweep.

The sixth case this session where a check BEFORE the fix dropped a hypothesis. Here it was
dropped by simply reading the source, not by a run -- that's cheaper than a measurement and
should come first.

## ⭐ ARCHITECTURE OF THE STALL: TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTE PIPELINES (2026-08-26)

Settled by READING, without a run -- the contradiction "plan=229 while navRes=0" resolved.

`FastPlanner.plan` has FOUR callers: `PathFinder:1240`, `FastNavigator:604`,
`FollowEntityTask:351` and `:513`. During the stall the task was "get a pickaxe", not
chasing an entity, and `navRes=0` -- meaning the plans came from the PHYSICAL pathfinder.

And they aren't DISCARDED there:

```java
boolean acceptable = fast.complete || arrivesAnyway || fastGuidePartial;
if (acceptable && fast.path.size() >= 2)
    return truncateAtBreaks(Optional.of(fast.toBlockNodes(goal, player)));
```

I.e. the 229 routes of 48 cells become a BLOCK GUIDE for physics.

IN TOTAL, DURING THE STALL, TWO PIPELINES WERE RUNNING, INDEPENDENTLY:
  physical -- received GOOD guides and emitted nothing (`tryEmit`=0 earlier);
  walking  -- received DEGENERATE routes from the combat BFS (`mqRefused(short)=2337`).

This explains the series' central paradox: planning is healthy, but the bot stands still. No
fix IN THE PLANNER will move this -- it's the route's CONSUMERS that disagree.

NEXT PASS: catch a stall with the `cp` instrument in hand (a healthy-run baseline already
exists: `cp=107/39/0/889/889`, zero duplicates) and see what the combat BFS's output turns
into exactly there. That will show whether to fix its budget or switch the walking pipeline
onto `FastPlanner`'s route.

## ⭐⭐⭐ IDLE TIME 49% -> 8%: THE CHASE FOR A SINGLE ITEM IS CAPPED (2026-08-26)

```

after the pit  median ~21%,  worst 85%
NOW           8%   8%   4%      gave3 -- the cap really fires
GATES        nav 14/14,  craft 21/22 with zero gate failures
```

CAUSE: `dc=12145/1/0/0/0/same12070` -- out of 12145 ticks, the choosing task picked the SAME
goal (a cobblestone block two blocks under the bot) 12070 times and never once gave up on
it. It had no give-up condition at all. Navigation was healthy meanwhile (`cp` with no
scraps, `mqRefused=3`, `pdWalking=446`) -- no pathfinder fix could have moved this.

THREE ATTEMPTS, THE SAME TRAP EACH TIME (record it and don't repeat):
  1. comparing the goal BY REFERENCE -- the tracker returns a new object for the same item,
     the clock resets every tick.            gave0
  2. the clock in INSTANCE FIELDS -- the task gets recreated, the budget goes with it.
     This is the exact bug I fixed for item pickup earlier in the session.   gave0
  3. my own "got closer -> reset the count" rule is too generous: the bot circles the item
     and keeps setting new proximity records.                                gave0
  4. a hard cap of 3 minutes per goal, reset ONLY by a change of goal.        gave3

GENERAL PRINCIPLE, CONFIRMED THREE TIMES: the budget belongs to the GOAL, not the task, and
must not be reset by anything except a change of goal. Each failure was caught by the
`gave<N>` counter BEFORE the fix was recorded as a success.

## ⭐ CORRECTION: THE CHASE CAP DOESN'T FIRE BECAUSE IT SHOULDN'T (2026-08-26)

Yesterday I recorded `gave0` as "the fix doesn't execute". Measuring the reset cause
disproves that:

```
same6806/gave3/rst45@100cm
   same object 6806 times,  give-ups 3,  CLOCK RESETS 45,
   the last reset was triggered by the goal "jumping" exactly 100 cm
```

Exactly ONE BLOCK is not item drift, it's a GRID STEP: the bot finished mining a block and
moved to the neighboring one. The goal changes LEGITIMATELY, and resetting the count in this
case is CORRECT.

So the cap behaves as intended: stays silent while goals honestly rotate (an ore vein, a
tree), and fires when one goal genuinely holds the bot -- the `same12070` case, which did
give `gave3`.

CONCLUSION FOR THE METHOD: "the counter reads zero" does NOT always mean "the code doesn't
execute". Sometimes it means "the condition correctly never occurred". The two can only be
told apart with a counter on the CAUSE, not on the fact. Here it cost one measurement and
removed a false conclusion.

Idle time in this batch: 4% and 39%.

## ⛔⛔ BENCH TRAP: THE CONFIG SURVIVES A ROLLBACK IN THE SOURCE (2026-08-27)

Disabled `breakGoalIsReach` in the source, built, deployed -- and the very next chain poll
showed the ENABLED-FLAG BRANCH (`Getting within 3 blocks of`, `DestroyBlockTask:713`). A
check explained it:

```
deploy/run/data/tester1/config/tungsten.json:  "breakGoalIsReach": true
deploy/run/data/tester2/config/tungsten.json:  "breakGoalIsReach": true
```

The mod READS the bench's config rather than overwriting it from defaults. So flipping the
flag in the source + build + deploy does NOT CHANGE the bench's behavior if the flag is
already written into the json. Brought both configs in line (false) and redeployed.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE MEASUREMENTS:
  - the "no flag" baseline runs (5 5 5 3 5 rungs) were taken BEFORE it was enabled --
    correct;
  - the run with 20.9% on the dominant leaf ran WITH THE FLAG ENABLED even though I thought
    it was off. As a comparison it's NO GOOD and doesn't feed the conclusions.

RULE FOR THE FUTURE: after changing a flag, CHECK
`deploy/run/data/*/config/tungsten.json`, don't trust the source. This session I've been
caught three times by "measuring with stale flags", and this is a fourth case of the same
class -- but caught before publishing a conclusion.

## ⭐⭐ THE SHUTTLE MEASURED: THE TASK CHAIN RESETS 59% OF THE TIME (2026-08-27)

The operator described it from the video: the bot goes to break a block, leaves to pick

```
  15  (no task)             ->  Getting to block ...
  10  Getting to block X    ->  Getting to block Y
(no task) occupies 29% of all samples
```

THIS IS TWO DIFFERENT PHENOMENA, not one:

     the task gets recreated from scratch. Almost a third of the run has no task at all.
  2. GOAL CHANGE -- 10 switches, block X to block Y: the very same running between positions.

INCIDENTALLY SOLVED AN OLD MYSTERY: I ran into budgets in INSTANCE FIELDS resetting three
times (item pickup, nearest-object selection, the idle clock). Now it's clear why: tasks
REALLY ARE being recreated constantly, and now there's a number for it.

against 10) and explains why any state inside a task is unreliable. Start with whoever

## ⛔ THE FREEZE EXPLAINED: A LATCH WHOSE KEY WAS LOCKED BEHIND IT (2026-08-28)

The user's complaint "stared at one spot and stopped for 3-5 minutes" has a precise cause.
`barrenStreak` grows ONLY when an ENTITY capture expires without closing distance, and only
resets on a successful capture or the start of a new one. But the gate sat in `tryPathTo`
and cut EVERYONE, including wandering. Two failed pursuits -> counter reaches 2 -> wandering
refused -> the bot doesn't move -> no new captures come in -> nobody resets it. Till the
run ends.

```

wanderTung = 1449/24 goals chosen / accepted
wander = 7047 ticks, wanderMoved = 64   -> the body moves 0.9% of ticks
```

Paired A/B: idle 62->38% and 15->0% in pairs where the latch DID ARM; the third pair
(`tp=0/0/0/0`) says nothing about the flag. The gate is now only for entity captures.

`tryExecutePath` is only reachable from `isPathComplete`, meaning the node has ALREADY

## ⛔ THE CHAIN CLOSED AT createNode: IT REJECTS ALMOST EVERYTHING (2026-08-25)

    children = 168/82/82   raw / valid / inserted, across 131 coarse searches
                           = ONE raw move per node

The generator is NOT the bottleneck: it enumerates forward/right/left across a yaw-scan
window of desiredYaw +/- 134.4 degrees in 22.5-degree steps, with and without sprint --
dozens of candidates per node. And rawChildren counts what the method RETURNED, i.e. already
after the "if (n != null)" filter.

So createNode returns null for almost everything -- on flat ground with no obstacles.

THE FULL CHAIN, FROM SYMPTOM TO ROOT:

    the generator offers dozens -> createNode rejects almost all -> one survives
    -> the search has nothing to branch on -> exhaustion -> no route is produced -> the
    executor has nothing to execute -> the bot stands still

This is one root for: the stall at 1219.5,104.1,-843.5, 135 mining ticks without a step, and
wander_recovery with wanderMoved=0.0 on flat ground.

⛔ SEPARATELY -- A MISTAKE IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT, CAUGHT BY ITSELF. An earlier measurement gave
children=0 and I concluded "no successors are generated." The counter sat in a branch that
only runs when there are >25 valid successors from a single expansion; real ones give two or
three, so the other branch always ran instead. The zero is retracted, the counter moved.

NEXT MEASUREMENT, AND IT'S A SMALL ONE: which exact check inside createNode rejects. Move
simulation is the last unmeasured link.

## ⛔ THE POST-MINING RESUME FIX -- THE MECHANISM IS CORRECT, IT DOESN'T CURE THE STALL

`resumeGotoAfterMining` gates on `TungstenMod.TARGET`, which is only set by manual entries
(`;goto`, a keybind, following, py4j). The altoclef drive -- the one that runs the ENTIRE
playthrough -- doesn't set it. So the resume after every mining run was exiting on the first
line.

mining completions -- i.e. it fixes genuinely dead code. But `mqSteps=0`, `pdWalking=0`: the
cycle changed from "mined -> nobody resumed" to "mined -> resumed -> mined again." The stall
isn't cured. The flag is DISABLED pending a separate measurement on a healthy craft run.

    [Tungsten] Mining done -- passage open                  <- mining runs and COMPLETES

The loop closes inside `PathFinder.search`, in the "Already standing at the wall" branch:

    EXECUTOR.startBreaking(pendingBreaks);

empty path -> kicks off a new search -> that search finds a short path to the same wall
again -> breaks it again. "A retry that will handle the rest" feeds into the same branch.

## ⛔ THE CEILING CHAIN CLOSED (2026-08-24)

Task priorities (BeatMinecraftTask):

    coal and iron ore   1050      getOrePriorityTask(...)
    stone tool set       520      addStoneToolsTasks()

Ore is TWICE as high-priority as the tool set. So the bot sits on the tool set not because it
blocks, but because the ore task NEVER ACTIVATES: its priority is computed by
`DistanceOrePriorityCalculator` -- from distance to the ore. No known ore -- no priority.

WHERE THE BOT IS AFTER STONE TOOLS (29 runs, 862 position samples):

    median Y = 82        min 54     max 136
    below Y=60:  22 of 862  =  2.6%

    Y 120-139     55
    Y 100-119    185
    Y  80-99     259
    Y  60-79     341
    Y  40-59      22

97.4% of the remaining run is above Y=60.

⛔ AND HERE'S WHAT THESE NUMBERS DON'T YET PROVE, so the next reader doesn't mistake
convenience for truth. In 1.18+ coal also generates HIGH (up to Y≈190, peak around Y=95),
and iron too has two bands. So "the bot doesn't go down" does NOT automatically mean "there's
no ore nearby." At a median Y=82, coal could easily be two steps away.

THE MISSING LINK, AND THERE'S ONLY ONE: whether the scanner sees ore at all. A counter is
needed: "how many times did coal_ore / iron_ore land in BlockScanner and at what distance."
Until it exists, there are two equally valid explanations, and they call for DIFFERENT fixes:

  (a) there's no ore nearby  ->  need the ability to go DOWN / search caves;
  (b) ore is nearby but not seen  ->  it's the scanner/radius, and going down won't help.

NEXT PASS: this counter first, then a fix. Exactly the rule that already saved a fifth empty
guess today.

## OPERATOR VIDEO REVIEW -- THREE GLITCHES, ONE CLASS OF BUG (2026-08-23)

The operator watched a run recording and named three things. Dissected one by one; TWO OF
THE THREE turned out to be the same defect -- **two owners write the same field every tick,
the last one wins**.

### 1. "Turns the camera one way while the block breaks another" -- FOUND, FIXED

Mechanism: `DestroyBlockTask` stamps `minerAimUntilMs` every tick and aims at the block.
`PathExecutor:465` does `player.setYaw(node.input.yaw)` on every path playback tick -- i.e.
it pulls the camera toward the next waypoint. Both write yaw/pitch, whoever writes last wins.

⛔ **The claim was read by exactly ONE consumer -- `BlockPathWalker` (the
`walkerYieldsToMiner` flag), and it doesn't move the camera.** The one that does move it knew
nothing about the claim. Hence the raycast misses I'd spent three passes explaining by
geometry (self-floor, a phantom target -- all disproved).

Fix: `executorYieldsAimToMiner` -- the executor hands the camera to the aim, and re-expresses
the keys into the actual reference frame (`reframeMovement`), preserving the world-space
direction of travel. This is NOT new machinery: the same file already solved this for the
BOW twelve lines above, it just never extended past `BowShooter.isActive()`. Counter:
`execYieldMiner`.

Side conclusion: `walkerYieldsToMiner` was measured honestly and showed zero -- because the
wrong component was the one yielding.

### 2. "Twitches back and forth" -- THE SAME DEFECT

The twitching is exactly the visual trace of the fight over camera and keys: the aim pulls
toward the block, the executor pulls along the route, the body shakes between them. Not
looking for a separate cause until item 1 is measured.

### ⛔ RETRACTING MY OWN "PROOF" ABOUT BARITONE (same day)

I recorded in a commit that `_Bari` in a lock trace was proof that the legacy engine had
driven the approach to an item. **THIS IS WRONG.** `owner` in the trace is a task's
`toString()`, truncated to 44 characters (`TungstenHelper:417`). The full string:

    GetToEntityTask:773  "Baritone stuck -> Tungsten locked for 30s"

So `_Bari` is the label of the RECOVERY state after getting stuck, not the driver; the
neighboring `_Tung` is a truncation of "Tungsten...". Read from a substring exactly the way
the checklist forbids (it's already recorded there: `rt=0/0/0` turned out to be the tail end
of `hurt=0/0/0`).

The operator's claim about baritone is STILL neither confirmed NOR disproved by a number:
`pdLegacy=0` in all four runs, the `legacyDrive` instrument has just been shipped and hasn't

### ⛔ AND A SECOND MISTAKE OF MINE: I WAS MEASURING WITH FLAGS I THOUGHT WERE OFF

`dbNoRetreat=1719`, `dbStepOver=1719` in run 4 -- both "self-floor" fixes, measured as

Three choice samples: `of=1`, `of=1`, `of=2` -- and in the one case with an alternative the
cheap one was taken (6 against 26). The ranking behaves sensibly.

the descent price wouldn't have changed anything: there was nothing to choose from (`of=1`).

⭐ SO THE FIX IS A GIVE-UP RULE, NOT A PRICE. A limit is needed: how much the bot is willing
to spend on ONE drop before marking it unreachable and getting on with business. Blocks
already have such a rule (`requestBlockUnreachable` after three far-away give-ups,
`farGiveUpRetriesFirst`); ITEMS apparently don't.

<!-- DESCENT-IS-PRICED-AS-A-FALL -->
## WHY A DROP AT THE BOTTOM OF A CAVE LOOKS LIKE A CHEAP GOAL (2026-08-23, answered by numbers)

Drops are ranked by `BaritoneHelper.calculateGenericHeuristic`, and its height term is this:

    if (yDiff > 0)  return distanceToTicks(2) / 2 * yDiff;               DESCENT ~4.8 ticks/block
    if (yDiff < 0)  return -yDiff * (JUMP_ONE_BLOCK + PLACE_ONE_BLOCK);  ASCENT  ~23 ticks/block

Descending is FIVE TIMES cheaper per block than ascending, because the model treats descent as
FALLING. For that drop (h=34, dy=-24) that's roughly 115 ticks for the descent against 170 for
the horizontal -- depth is barely penalized, and an item at the bottom of a cave beats out
closer targets.

⛔ BUT THE BOT DOESN'T FALL. To get 24 blocks down it has to dig or find a way down, and that
costs disproportionately more than "half a fall from two blocks" per block. The heuristic is
correct for a pathfinder that CAN fall; for TARGET SELECTION it underestimates depth.

This answers the previous pass's question. Deliberately NOT building a fix this pass: two
fixes in a row in this area were built from reading the code and didn't fire once (`shKept=0`,
`fixKept=0`). Before changing the price, it needs to be CHECKED on a run that the drop
actually beat a nearer target, rather than being the only one known.

The distribution is BIMODAL AND WITHIN A SINGLE BUILD: a run either reaches about a third of
its targets, or none at all. So this is NOT a regression from shipped flags (that would be

A run that reaches nothing can mine nothing -- hence the zero rungs. This is P1/P2 in its
pure form: getting stuck on standard terrain, not an arena edge case.

RETRACTING A CONCLUSION OF MY OWN, MADE AN HOUR EARLIER. I recorded here that the ceiling was
a blocked line of sight, based on rayOther=5012 / rayMiss=4128 / rayLeaves=1923. This was a
WRONG ATTRIBUTION. The raycast counters are STATIC and SHARED across all callers, and the

distSq<=16 and CORRECTLY didn't fire: the bot wasn't near the tree, it was far from it. At
that distance the ray measures distance, not canopy. Fixing the view would have treated the
symptom of the wrong illness.

removed 73.6s of standing still per run (t=-2.16, established) at zero rungs; route

## ⭐⭐⭐ P3 MEASURED: REMOVING BARITONE IS 5 FILES, AND THE BLOCKER ISN'T IN THE CODE (2026-08-20)

An inventory instead of an eyeball estimate. All of altoclef takes from `baritone.*` (i.e.
from shredder, since `baritone/` doesn't compile) exactly **11 imports across 5 files**:

    AltoClef.java              Baritone, BaritoneAPI, api.Settings, altoclef.AltoClefSettings
    BotBehaviour.java          api.Settings, altoclef.AltoClefSettings, api.utils.RayTraceUtils
    TabCompleter.java          TabCompleteHelper, TabCompleteEvent, AbstractGameEventListener
    ClientTickMixin.java       BaritoneAPI, WorldEvent, EventState
    CustomBaritoneGoalTask.java  api.pathing.goals.Goal

And only ONE of the five has anything to do with pathfinding:

  - `ClientTickMixin` only forwards WorldEvent to shredder's handler so its chunk cache stays
    alive. Dies with shredder, needs no replacement.
  - `TabCompleter` -- command autocomplete. Zero relation to pathfinding.
  - `BotBehaviour` / `AltoClef` -- settings (`initializeBaritoneSettings`, syncing
    `acceptableThrowawayItems`) plus one utility, `RayTraceUtils`. Plumbing, not an engine.
  - `CustomBaritoneGoalTask` -- the only real one: it holds BOTH goal types, `Goal cachedGoal`
    (baritone) and `AltoGoal cachedAlto` (tungsten). I.e. the tungsten branch already exists
    there, and the baritone branch is the legacy half of a two-path class.

⭐ **THE MAIN POINT: SHREDDER IS NO LONGER DRIVING THE BOT.** This same class carries a
`pdLegacy` counter -- "ticks where the goal was handed to the LEGACY engine because tungsten
refused." Across every run of this pass it reads **`pdLegacy=0`**: on arenas shredder never
gets the goal, not once.

⛔ **SO THE P3 BLOCKER ISN'T A REFACTOR, IT'S P1/P2.** Deleting five files is cheap; the risky
part is something else -- removing the fallback the bot lands on wherever tungsten refuses. So
the order is:

    per task tick   bot 333/785 = 42%           victim 414/2774 = 15%   (bot ahead)

counters cannot answer it; what is needed is an explicit ALIVE-AND-FIGHTING tick count.

⭐⭐ BUILT, AND IT CLOSES THE LEAD. fightTicks counts ticks with a live target at the single entry
every fight passes through, so contact fraction means the same thing for both fighters:

    victim   contact 434 of 586             = 74%

Identical. The raw 333-against-414 gap was only that the victim's fight RAN LONGER -- 586 ticks

and with it the last "difference still standing" on this course.

⛔ EIGHT CANDIDATES NOW ELIMINATED WITH NUMBERS on allround: aim, approach, the bow's camera, the

    victim   landed=71  crits=24    ready=132/81/0/128

16-17 deaths. Sixty-eight connects with twenty-nine crits is arithmetically about seventeen kills
against a twenty-HP target; the bot books eleven.

⭐⭐ ANSWERED FROM THE SOURCE, AND IT IS THE FIRST HALF: a "landed" swing is NOT a hit. TriggerBot:

    lifetimeHits++;
    mc.interactionManager.attackEntity(player, target);

The counter increments BEFORE the attack is sent, so it counts swings ISSUED -- misses, swings out
of reach and swings into air all included. `crits` likewise counts swings made in a crit condition,
not crit damage delivered.

So "both connect about seventy times and the bot crits more" is not evidence about damage at all.
It is the same class of error as angleMean: a counter whose name promises more than it measures,
and the FIFTH such counter caught this session.

⛔ THEREFORE the real damage question is still unmeasured, and the counter for it already exists --
`dealt` in placeStats, which the course does not print. Adding it to allround's readout is the next
step; no behaviour needs touching to learn this.

So what loses allround is still open, and it is NOT: the aim (angle refused 5 swings of 566), the
approach (forward pressed on 64 of 77 ready-far ticks), the bow's camera, the bow's draw, reach
control, standing still, or the weapon in hand. That is a lot of the space eliminated with numbers,

## ⭐⭐⭐ TEN TO EIGHTEEN SAMPLES PER RUN INSTEAD OF ONE (dbTargets, 2026-08-19)

The cost of a playthrough question was the whole problem: six flags were each judged on six runs
and three of those verdicts later reversed. Two ways out were tried and both refused by
measurement -- halving the watch window (loses the signal, saves 2x) and cutting per-run overhead
(there is none: a 350 s run is rcon 1 s, connect 22 s, reset 11 s, start 4 s, WATCH 313 s = 89%).

The third way is in the same numbers: a run does not attempt one block, it attempts dozens.

    FAIL   closest 9.8   dbTargets=10/0    arrival  0%
    PASS   closest 4.2   dbTargets=18/2    arrival 11%
    PASS   closest 0.7   dbTargets=14/8    arrival 57%

Ten to eighteen targets per run, and the arrival rate tracks the verdict monotonically. Three runs
now yield about forty samples instead of three, so six runs per arm is roughly ninety samples per
arm -- which is the difference between "this flag needs four hours" and "this flag can be answered
this afternoon".

A target counts as REACHED the moment the bot is inside 4.5 blocks of it: vanilla reach, the same
line PASS and FAIL already turn on (no failing run today ever got inside 4.4, every passing one got
inside 1.3).

⛔ USE THIS, NOT THE RUNG COUNT, for anything judged on the playthrough from here. The rung count
is one coarse number per six minutes on a population whose spread swamps every effect measured
today; this is tens of numbers from the same six minutes, on the exact quantity that separates a
run that works from one that does not.

<!-- G-1.914 -->
## ⛔ THE CHEAP PROXY DOES NOT WORK: HALVING THE RUN LOSES THE SIGNAL (2026-08-19)

The entry below says this flag needs n=20+ per arm "or a cheaper proxy than a nine-minute run".
The obvious proxy -- halve the watch window -- was tried and refused by measurement.

    standard runs (5 min)   closest approach 0.2 0.3 1.3 4.4 6.0 12.3   arrived(<2) 3/6
    halved runs (2.5 min)   closest approach 1.6 3.6 4.3 4.7 4.9 5.3 6.3 6.7   arrived(<2) 1/8

The short runs collapse toward one side: the distribution stops being "some runs arrive, some
never do" and becomes "almost nothing has arrived YET". That is a different quantity -- it measures
how far the bot has got by 2.5 minutes, not whether it can get there at all -- so a flag judged on
it would be judged on run-up speed rather than on capability.

And the saving is smaller than it looks: eight 2.5-minute runs took 25.8 minutes wall clock against
roughly 50 for eight full ones, because connect, reset and teardown dominate a short run. Half the
cost for a metric that no longer answers the question is not a trade worth making.

⭐ WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY BE CHEAPER, recorded for the next attempt rather than tried blind: cut the
PER-RUN OVERHEAD, not the watch window. A sweep pays connect + kill/respawn/heal + fresh-start
search + teardown on every single run, and those are fixed costs that a shorter window cannot
touch. Reusing one client session across several samples would cut more than halving the window
does, and without changing what is being measured.

## ⭐⭐⭐ A GATE THAT SEPARATES 6/6: HOW CLOSE THE BOT GETS TO THE BLOCK IT WANTS

Six playthrough runs on the shipped default, closest approach to the block DestroyBlockTask is
working on, against the verdict:

    PASS  5 rungs   1.3 blocks        FAIL  0 rungs   12.3 blocks
    PASS  5 rungs   0.3 blocks        FAIL  0 rungs    6.0 blocks
    PASS  3 rungs   0.2 blocks        FAIL  0 rungs    4.4 blocks

No overlap. Every passing run arrives inside 1.3 blocks; no failing run ever gets inside 4.4 --
i.e. never inside the 4.5 reach, for the whole run. The zero-rung failure is "never arrives",
full stop. It is NOT "arrives and cannot mine", which is what the blocked-ray counters
(rayOther in the thousands) had suggested and which would have wanted the opposite fix.

⭐⭐ AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT PROBLEM SOLVED, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE FINDING. The entry
above records that six flags were A/B'd at n=6 and none separated, because rungs-reached is a
coarse count on a population whose spread swamps any effect. dbBestDist is CONTINUOUS, it is
recorded every run, and it separates cleanly at n=6. Future playthrough work is judged against
this rather than against the ladder: it answers in six runs what the rung count could not answer
in sixty-four.

⛔ WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN: why the approach never happens on those runs. All the pathing flags

Six mechanisms were built, gated and A/B'd against this, each with a counter proving it executed

⛔ THE CONCLUSION IS ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM, NOT ABOUT THE FLAGS. Each of these fixed a
REAL, measured defect -- routes truncated at an unplayable edge, a task that cannot tell moving
from approaching, a fall guard that truncated its own simulation -- and the ladder still sits at
two to three rungs. Whatever caps the playthrough is not any single one of them, and the
distribution says why it is hard to see: eighteen runs reach ZERO rungs and one reaches six, on
identical settings. The spread between neighbouring runs is larger than any effect measured today.

⛔ SO THE NEXT PASS SHOULD NOT BE A SEVENTH FLAG. Two things follow from the numbers:
  1. n=6 per arm cannot resolve anything smaller than a ~2x change on this bench. Either the
     measurement gets cheaper (shorter runs, a tighter gate than "rungs reached") or arms need
     n=20+, which is four hours per question.
  2. The 0-rung runs are 28% of all runs and they are a different failure from the 3-4 rung ones.
     Splitting THOSE by cause -- rather than averaging them together -- is where the next signal
     is, because a fix for the median run is being judged against a population that contains a
     quarter of runs that never started.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE PLAYTHROUGH'S WALL, MEASURED: 27 OF 28 ROUTES ARE TRUNCATED FOR A MISSING MOVEMENT

Full counter capture from a stalled playthrough run (deploy/runner/freezes/stall_run4_ladder.txt),
task chain sitting on {@code <Getting to block 74,127,-57> Tungsten (primary) walking terrain}:

    mqStarted=28   mqSteps=25   mqTicks=3207   qNoMove=25   mqNoClass=27
    pdEnter=3227   pdStuck=10   pdStallReset=30   srch=0/0/0   scan=47851

The movement queue started 28 times and advanced 25 steps in 160 seconds -- about ONE step per
start -- and {@code mqNoClass=27} says why: 27 of those 28 chains were TRUNCATED because an edge in
the route had no movement class. MovementQueue classifies each edge as swim / pillar / diagonal /
ascend / descend / fall / traverse, and anything else is handed back. What falls through is
PARKOUR -- a running jump. The file records the measured shape from a live @gamer run:
{90,134,-36} -> {86,135,-34}, four blocks across and one up.

So the block-space search plans routes the physics executor cannot play. The queue honestly runs
the prefix it has movements for -- usually one step -- stops, the route is replanned identically,
and the bot spends its run re-walking the same first step. That is not "the bot is stuck", not
"the search is slow" (bs=29/29/170/170@4265ms is the BlockScanner's total rescan cost for the whole
run, ~147 ms each, and I misread it as per-search before checking), and not damage (dmgWhy read
0/0/0/0/0 with dmgTaken=0.0 on two of the failing runs).

⭐ THE FIX IS A CAPABILITY, NOT A PATCH: implement MovementParkour so the queue can execute the
edges the search already emits. The alternative -- teach the search not to emit them -- throws away
routes that are genuinely the only way across, and the file's own comment says the truncation was
meant to hand off to the walker, which measurably is not getting there.

WHY nav_gaps IS GREEN AND THIS IS NOT: nav_gaps offers 2, 3 and 4-block gaps on a FLAT arena, where
the route can be a straight line of traverse edges and the walker's sprint-jump covers the rest.
Real terrain puts the jump in the middle of a route with height changes on both sides, which is the
shape that has no class.

    CHAIN  Collecting [[wooden_pickaxe]] -> {stick x 2} -> Craft 2x2 {dark_oak_planks x 2}
           -> "Moving item to slot..."      six levels deep, in the GRID, not in navigation

    mc=3080/0/0/2/0    fill/short/out/wait/invalid -- it FILLS, 3080 times
    mcFlight=73        NON-ZERO
    ciTick=6698  ciReceive=25  ciGrid=0    cgTick=0  cgSent=0

CraftGenericManuallyTask asked "which of the five it does every tick decides what to read next,

    MOVEMISMATCH holding=oak_planks      want=[stick] dest=CraftingTableSlot{slot 4}

⭐⭐ THE FACT IS IN, AND THE FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG. entityCloseWalk now counts

    FAIL   724/462/33    moved on 462 ticks, got CLOSER on 33 of them   (7%)
    PASS   241/123/6     moved on 123, closer on 6                      (5%)
    PASS   5/4/4         moved on 4, closer on 4                       (100%)

A brief firing closes distance on every tick and the run passes. A long one moves constantly and
closes on one tick in fifteen. So the bot WALKS AND DOES NOT APPROACH -- which is a third thing,
and neither of the two candidates I had. Not "the inputs are stolen" (it moves) and not "the drop
is unreachable from above" (a short walk reaches it fine). Either the aim is overwritten each tick
so hold(MOVE_FORWARD) carries it wherever it faces, or it is pressed against geometry and sliding
along it -- 462 moving ticks for 33 closer looks like sliding on a wall.

And the fourth field settles WHY, ticks/moved/closer/aimed (aimed read at the start of a tick, so
it reports what the previous tick left behind; lookAt SNAPS yaw, so the bot points at the drop by
construction after this branch runs):

    FAIL   482/323/6/321    aimed on 321 of 482, moved 323, closed 6
    FAIL   241/237/3/6      aimed on 6 of 241, moved 237, closed 3
    PASS   362/183/4/182    aimed 182, moved 183, closed 4

The first line is the answer: CORRECTLY AIMED, MOVING, AND NOT CLOSING. 321 aimed ticks and 323
moving ticks produced six that got nearer. A body that faces its target, walks, and does not
arrive is pressed against geometry and sliding along it. The second line is a second mode, where
the yaw is overwritten almost entirely (6 of 241) and holding forward carries the bot wherever
that leaves it facing.

⛔ SO THE APPROACH DOES NOT FAIL BY DECIDING WRONGLY, AND NO INPUT HACK CAN FIX IT. Walking is not
a route. The drop sits one block below the surface in the hole the bot just dug, and reaching it
needs a real short-range path that DESCENDS into that excavation. That is core movement work and
it is the honest next task -- not a sixth flag on GetToEntityTask.

Everything measured now agrees on that. pickup_pit passes because its pit is a clean 1x1 in flat
ground the bot can walk down into; the failing course's hole is whatever its own mining left, and
a horizontal walk at a drop sitting one block below the surface just carries the bot across the
top of it. So the fix belongs in how the approach DESCENDS into an excavation -- not in whether it
decides to approach, which is where all four earlier passes were looking.

Also eliminated by building the geometry directly, one variable at a time, all green:

    stall can never be noticed) and it returns early (so the recovery below it is unreachable).
    `isActive()` is `PATHFINDER.active` OR `isExecutorRunning()`, i.e. TRUE while the pathfinder
    is merely LOOKING.

    — that one governs MineAndCollectTask, and turning it on for this would change two behaviours
    in one measurement). A search that has not moved the body for 6 s — MovementProgressChecker's
    own default — is released via `TungstenHelper.stop()` so the approach can be planned afresh.

    MAX_BARREN_LOCKS is 2, so two barren locks should make tryPathTo refuse. The run read
    lock=49/0/50 -- FORTY-NINE barren locks and no refusal. The cause is in tryPathToEntity:

        if (!entity.equals(lockedEntity)) barrenStreak = 0;   // "a new target is a new problem"

    This course wants TWO diamonds. Alternating between two drops it cannot reach resets the streak
    on every switch, so the escalation can never reach 2. The comment is right that a NEW target is

      approach went 11.57 -> 3.60 in 24 ticks (0.33 blocks/tick, the sprint limit) — i.e. arrived

          fight ~150 ticks / shot cycle ~40  =>  3-4 arrows per fight
          skeleton hit rate 30-38%           =>  roughly one connects
          the gate allows ZERO
          P(pass) = P(all 3-4 arrows miss) ~ 20%   <- and the measured pass rate is 20% over 287 runs

      EVERY shot across an open 12-block field. Five approach flags are closed (each measured a
