- [ ] **THE BOW: TWO RED COURSES FAIL FOR DIFFERENT REASONS, AND ONE OF THEM DOESN'T SHOOT AT ALL

      ⚠️ CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM 2026-08-14 (G-1.83, checked against the code): `RELEASE_CONE` IS
      NOT IN THE TREE. The constant is called `DRAW_START_CONE` (`BowShooter.java:31`), and its
      javadoc directly refutes the closure's wording: it "doesn't solve accuracy on release — it only
      keeps the draw from starting while the camera is still turning." That is, the fix is in place,
      but under a different name and with a corrected meaning. The item remains OPEN: shooting was
      closed, and the red course, as the item itself says, fails for reasons unrelated to it. The
      name is corrected here so the next reader doesn't grep for a ghost.
      (measured 2026-08-08 from artifacts ALREADY ON DISK, without a single run).**
      > **UPDATE 2026-08-10 (not rewriting the analysis below — it's about aim, and the mechanism
      > turned out to be different).** Deaths on `bow_flee` are not caused by shooting. Measured: the
      > bot was driving itself to the edge of the platform (every stall at radius 18.57-18.7 against
      > an edge of 20, keys held, the pursuer not in contact) and couldn't sprint, backing away while
      > facing the threat. Three fixes — the flee goal can move along the edge, the bow checks
      > distance every tick, fleeing reclaims the freed-up camera — brought stalls from 54 → 0/8/8/5,
      > sprint from 24% → 50-60%, median deaths from 6 → 4 (n=8 against n=9).
      > The course is still RED: the criterion is zero deaths. Separately refuted by experiment:
      > shooting less often doesn't buy survival (threshold 0.5→0.75 gave deaths 5/4/5 and hits
      > 0/0/0). Details — docs/ai/progress.md and tasks G-1.66/G-1.67.

      `bow_flee` and `bow_flee_hard` both give `hits=0`, and this looks like one disease. It isn't.
      Counted `BowShooter`'s own lines in `chat.txt` for two runs in a row:

          bow_flee        released 0 / 0     aborted 6 and 4     -> NOT ONE arrow in 60s
          bow_flee_hard   released 2 / 2     aborted 4 and 2     -> shoots and MISSES

      These are two different defects, and they need to be treated separately.

      📐 CANDIDATE MECHANISM (consistent with the code, NOT measured): a shot only fires if
      `chargeTicks >= CHARGE_TICKS(22)` AND the aim lands within `RELEASE_CONE = 3.5°`
      (`BowShooter.tick:124-127`). With `TIMEOUT_TICKS = 100`, a draw that doesn't hit the cone
      within 5s gets cancelled — that's the "aborted." The difference between the courses is exactly
      what such a mechanism would predict: in `bow_flee` the chase is SLOWED, the bot really is
      running and constantly turning — the aim never settles, 0 shots; in `bow_flee_hard` the chase
      is equal speed, the bot gets caught at 7.3s, and that's when it manages to aim — 2 shots.
      So the suspicion is: **the bot can't shoot WHILE MOVING**, and that's exactly what's needed to
      kite.

      ⛔ INSTRUMENT FIRST, THEN THE FIX (RULE ONE). A counter was already added this session:
      `bowShots` in `placeStats` (`BowShooter.getShotsFired()` existed, and NOBODY called it). The
      instrument's check is set IN ADVANCE: on `bow_flee` it must show 0, on `bow_flee_hard` — 2.
      Show something else — the instrument is lying, not the bot.
      ⚠️ AND DON'T FORGET: `ranged_moving` IS GREEN. So shooting as such works, and before touching
      the cone, it's necessary to understand what's different about `ranged_moving` — otherwise the
      fix will break a green course.

      ✅ THE DIFFERENCE IS FOUND, AND IT IS EXACTLY WHAT THE MECHANISM PREDICTED (read in
      `scenarios_pvp.py:438-470`): **IN `ranged_moving` THE TARGET MOVES, NOT THE BOT.** The course
      sends `@goto` ONLY TO THE VICTIM (it strafes along a lane), and gives the bot not a single
      movement command — it stands and shoots. In `bow_flee` it's the BOT ITSELF that's running.

      So three courses add up to one statement, and they don't contradict each other:

          ranged_moving    the bot STANDS, the target moves       GREEN, hits>=2 of 6
          bow_flee_hard    the bot is caught at 7.3s              2 shots (shoots once cornered)
          bow_flee         the bot RUNS the whole time            0 shots in 60s

      So the defect can be stated precisely: **the bot can shoot at a moving target, but it can't
      shoot WHILE MOVING ITSELF.** The aim never manages to settle into the cone while the pathfinder
      is turning the body.

      ⛔ AND FROM THIS — WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE: simply widen `RELEASE_CONE`. That would worsen
      accuracy where it's currently green (`ranged_moving` is judged on hits, not shots), i.e. trade
      a red course for a green one. What needs fixing is the "shooter is moving" case — e.g. measure
      aim error relative to the body's own rotation — not loosen the general threshold.

      ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-09. The diagnosis above was CORRECT, and shooting while moving is fixed.
      But the course's own failure turned out NOT to be about shooting, and that cost an evening —
      so the full outcome is here.

      **Shooting (fixed).** `RELEASE_CONE` was not widened, but REMOVED: release is now decided by
      a predicted hit — the shot is run through the same simulator from the current aim, and the
      arrow fires when the calculation predicts a hit. An angle can't be the threshold, because the
      lateral miss from an angle grows with range: 3.5° is 0.37 blocks at 6 and 1.53 at 25 against a
      target of ~0.6. Plus the bow no longer draws while turning is in progress (a drawn bow forbids
      sprinting), and the solver finally accounts for the shooter's own velocity, which vanilla adds
      to the arrow.
      Result: `bowShots` 0 → 7-9 per run, `ranged_moving` stayed green.

      **The course's failure (found, a different one).** What was wrecking the distance wasn't
      shooting, but the FRACTION OF TIME SPENT MOVING. The bot sprints 83% of the ticks it executes,
      but 40-45% of the course it STANDS pathfinding, and net displacement comes out to 41-57% of
      sprint speed — an effective 2.8 blocks/s against 4.8 for the slowed chase. That's why a
      caught-up bot never broke contact: 23 hits a minute at an average distance of 3.95. Fixed by
      having the bot move via keys while the next path is being computed: hits 23 → 17, damage
      120 → 92, `avg dist` out of a failing lane to 3 gates of 3.

      ⚠️ WHAT NOT TO DO (checked and rejected by measurement): changing the replanning frequency —
      the number of plans halved, but search time didn't change, and distance got worse; adding a
      footing check before moving blind — on flat ground it blocks 260-290 ticks per run and eats the
      whole gain; blaming the "corner-seeker" for contacts — the planner's goal really was a
      corner-seeker and was fixed (contacts moved from the field's borders inward), but it isn't what
      drives the bot's hit distance.

      ⛔ STAYS RED: deaths. With regeneration disabled (`arena.prepare(regen=False)`, done on
      purpose), the "0 deaths" gate literally means "take no more than THREE sword hits in 60s".
      Deaths are proportional to accumulated damage, not a separate disease: 92 damage = 4.6 lives,
      and the observed 4-6 deaths match this exactly. So what needs lowering is the number of hits,
      and that's what should be measured — the `dw=hits/damage/avgGap/maxGap` counter for this
      already exists and ticks from the client (altoclef's own `dmgTaken` is dead on these courses:
      its chain gets not a single tick, `mdCalls=0`).

<!-- G-1.49 -->
⭐⭐ **THE ROOT, NOT A THIRD PATCH: `LOAD_SENSITIVE` IS A HAND-MAINTAINED WORD LIST, AND IT KEEPS
FALLING "CLOSED".** (2026-08-08. Over the session I fixed it THREE TIMES: under nav, then under
craft, then under mob. That's a sign of a flawed design, not bad luck.)
The guard decides whether a failed gate can be blamed on low fps by COMPARING THE CRITERION'S NAME
TEXT against a set of substrings. So: phrase a new criterion in different words, and a starved run
silently turns into "the bot is broken." The error skews toward blaming the bot, i.e. the most
expensive direction.
Combing through all the suites (a blunt regex, some lines are `gate=False`, don't count those)
showed that WHOLE CLASSES of clearly load-sensitive gates sit outside the list, especially timing
ones:
  pvp:   `first landed swing <= 15s`, `contact <= 45s`, `kill <= 120s`, `crossed <= 60s`,
         `kill <= 150s`, `caught the runner (contact <= 120s)`, `survive >= 30s`
  craft: `time to the FIRST log`
  nav:   `took no damage`
  mob:   `the fight ran on tungsten` (see G-1.48 — also named incorrectly)
⛔ THE CORRECT FIX — NOT ADDING WORDS, BUT MOVING THE SIGNAL ONTO THE CRITERION ITSELF: give
`Criterion` a flag (e.g. `load_sensitive=True`), so that EVERY new gate declares this explicitly
when it's written, instead of retroactively through a substring list in another file. Then
forgetting it produces a visible error at the moment the course is written, rather than a silent
false red a month later.
⚠️ The fix is wide (touches all courses), so it should be done as a SEPARATE pass with a baseline
captured across all suites — don't bolt it onto the current measurement.

<!-- G-1.48 -->
⛔ **MY OWN FIX TO THE ALLOW-LIST TURNED OUT TO BE BASED ON A WRONG READING (2026-08-08).**
I did NOT add "ran on tungsten" to `LOAD_SENSITIVE`, on the grounds that: "`mdTung=0` means the
engine wasn't running, and that isn't excused by frame rate." Two hours later I found out for
myself that `mdTung=0` means something COMPLETELY DIFFERENT: a hit belongs to tungsten only AT
STRIKING DISTANCE, and the task drives everything before that. So `mdTung=0` is a proxy for "the
bot never closed the distance," and closing on a kiting skeleton at 8.7 fps is exactly what a slow
client gets in the way of.
CONSEQUENCE, VISIBLE IN THE NUMBERS: runs at **9.9 / 12.4 / 8.7 fps** were recorded as GENUINE
FAILs rather than INVALID, because this gate always fails and it isn't on the allow-list. The guard
can't mark a run invalid while even one failing gate is off the list.
✅ FIX IT LIKE THIS (once the rate is captured, so as not to change code mid-measurement): rename
the criterion to what it actually measures ("reached striking distance"), and ADD it to
`LOAD_SENSITIVE` — it is honestly load-sensitive.
⚠️ And this is already the SECOND time this session that an instrument fix rested on an earlier
reading of mine that I later disproved and DID NOT GO BACK TO FIX. The lesson isn't "fix instruments
less," it's "once you correct your understanding — go through everything built on it."

- [ ] **G-1.50 ⭐⭐ ALL REMAINING GOALS ARE OF ONE KIND, AND ARE CURED IN ONE PIECE (2026-08-08).**
      Took them apart one by one and saw the common thread: EVERY remaining goal is a PREDICATE, not a place.
        `EscapeFromWaterGoal.isInGoal`      = "not water and not next to water"
        `GoalRunAwayFromEntities`          = "further than N from all entities"
        `GoalDodgeProjectiles`             = "not on the arrow's line"
        lava                                = "not lava and not next to lava"
      baritone could EAT them as-is because it SEARCHED: a predicate is a perfectly normal goal function for
      A*. The tungsten drive can't do that: it STEERS TO A POINT. Hence `suggestFleePoint`, added
      last session with the measurement "368 of 596 entries lost, the bot stood still for 4 minutes", and my
      `AltoGoal.Flee` from today, where the caller computes the point.
      ⭐⭐ SO THE RIGHT SOLUTION IS NOT FOUR SEPARATE PORTS, BUT ONE SHAPE:
      `AltoGoal.NearestSatisfying(Predicate<BlockPos> ok, int maxRadius)` — expands outward around the
      player to the first cell where `ok` is true, and RETURNS IT as `target()`; `reached()` is the same
      predicate. Then water, lava, fleeing and dodging become FOUR CALLS, and the point search
      lives in ONE place where it can be made correct once (expansion step, radius limit,
      per-tick cache — so it doesn't scan 60 times a second).
      ⛔ THIS IS EXACTLY "A CORE FIX, NOT A PATCH" UNDER RULE 6 OF AGENTS.md: not propping up every goal
      with its own hack, but recognizing that the drive needs a point, and giving a common way to get one.
      ⛔ GATES: `nav_water` EXISTS and is GREEN (water is already ported, PASS at 16.2 fps).
      ✅ WATER DONE FIRST AND PASSED: `GetOutOfWaterTask` no longer holds baritone.
      ⛔⛔ LAVA IS A TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE COST A REGRESSION IF PORTED "LIKE WATER".
      `EscapeFromLavaGoal`'s heuristic has a line `isWater -> -100`: getting out of lava INTO water is
      STRONGLY PREFERRED (it extinguishes), and INDEPENDENT OF DISTANCE. `isInGoal`, meanwhile, is
      just "not lava and not next to lava".
      So a naive `NearestSatisfying(not-lava)` would send the BURNING bot to the nearest dry block
      instead of water three steps away. My own claim that "searching nearest expresses the same
      preference" is TRUE for water (there ranking is monotonic in distance) and FALSE here.
      ⭐ THE CORRECT PORT IS TWO STAGES: first `NearestSatisfying(isWater, r)`, and only if there's no water
      within radius — `NearestSatisfying(not-lava-and-not-next-to-lava, r)`. A predicate does not
      express preference; the ORDER OF CALLS does.
      ⛔ AND THE MAIN POINT ABOUT THE GATE: THERE IS NO LAVA COURSE IN ANY SUITE. So this is a behavior fix on
      the survival path that has nothing to verify it. Course first (`nav_lava`: bot in lava, with water and
      dry land nearby; gate — survived and NOT on fire), then the port. Same order that closed #37.

- [~] **G-1.4 PARTIAL (2026-08-03): `staleRoot 609 → 165`, NOT TO ZERO. THE SOLUTION WAS ALREADY WRITTEN.**
      ⛔ SELF-CORRECTION: the commit claimed "609 → 0" from ONE 8-minute run, where the walker
      was working almost the whole time. On a 15-minute run the honest number is **165**. The fix gives
      roughly a fourfold reduction, not zero, and that's what should have been claimed.
      THE REMAINING 165 is exactly the case I left as acceptable: NOBODY is leading the bot to the root
      (the walker isn't running), and arming the path then would mean hanging.
      ⛔⛔ MAIN CONCLUSION AFTER FULLY READING THE EXECUTOR (2026-08-03): THE REMAINING 165 IS
      NOT A DEFECT, IT'S CORRECT BEHAVIOR. `PathExecutor.tick` already contains a branch "the walker disappeared
      during arming → disarm and play from here" (a deliberate cure for
      fifteen six-second freezes on chase_terrain). So if the emission is skipped
      when there IS NO walker, `setPath` won't arm it (arming requires a walker), playback
      would start immediately from a foreign root and fail on drift at the first tick — exactly what
      the 2.0 check protects against.
      ⇒ THIS CANNOT BE FIXED WITH A TWEAK. It's the cost of the ARCHITECTURE: the executor only knows how to
      PLAY BACK A RECORDING. The remainder can be closed exactly one way — teach it to
      RE-SIMULATE the tail from the player's actual state. That's a separate architectural
      unit, not a one-line fix, and it should be taken up with a fresh context.
      ⛔ "JUST LAUNCH THE WALKER TO THE ROOT" — CHECKED AND THREE TIMES WORSE: `staleRoot 165 → 507`.
      Reason: `BlockPathWalker.start()` BEGINS WITH `stop()`, i.e. it resets whatever
      the walker was doing. Instead of waiting you get extra reshuffling: more replans,
      more stale roots. Option closed — the fourth in this line. What it needs is the
      remaining option from the list: teach the executor to RE-SIMULATE the tail from the player's
      actual state — then "someone has to walk the bot to the root" stops being a precondition.
      `PathExecutor.setPath` KNOWS how to handle a far root: it ARMS the path — doesn't play it, but waits
      for the WALKER to bring the bot to the root — and its own comment says arming
      exists precisely for this, and arming without a walker would mean hanging, not waiting.
      The check in `setCurrentPath` was firing EARLIER and discarding the emission, i.e. it duplicated
      this logic and never gave it a chance. Now the rejection is narrowed down to the case
      the executor genuinely can't survive: NOBODY is leading the bot to the root.
      ⛔ WHY THREE ATTEMPTS BEFORE THIS FAILED — one reason for all of them: they treated a far
      root as an ERROR to prevent, whereas the executor treats it as a
      SITUATION to wait out.
      (historical entry below — three discarded options with numbers)

- [~] **G-1.4 (2026-08-03) 374 "stale-rooted path emission" REJECTIONS — HISTORY OF ATTEMPTS.** While the search is thinking, the bot keeps moving, the path's root goes stale,
      and all the search's work gets thrown away: 374 rejections in a live run.
      ⛔ THE ATTEMPT "trim the path to the closest node and hand off the tail" WAS MEASURED AND ROLLED BACK:
      nav 10/12, `nav_flat` and `nav_staircase` red (8 and 12 freezes on FLAT ground);
      without it, 11/12. REASON: this executor doesn't follow waypoints, it PLAYS BACK
      RECORDED INPUTS from the first node. Starting mid-way gives inputs recorded for a body
      that was already moving — foreign speed and state, instant drift. The point list
      can be re-rooted, the RECORDING cannot.
      ⛔ THE SECOND ATTEMPT ALSO DIDN'T WORK, AND NOW IT'S MEASURED. Re-rooting the NEXT
      search to the player's position (`overrideStartPos`) gave **staleRoot=609 over 8 minutes**. The first
      "0 rejections" after that fix was simply `verboseDebugLogging` being off — I
      flagged this in the commit as "suggestive, not conclusive", and the caveat turned out right,
      the conclusion didn't.
      ⛔ WHY IT DOESN'T WORK: re-rooting at the moment of REJECTION doesn't help if the next search
      takes longer than it takes the bot to move two blocks. It's the same race.
      THE RIGHT DIRECTION (three options remain, all need measurement via `staleRoot=`):
        (a) ⛔ ROOTING AT A PREDICTED POSITION — CHECKED AND WORSE: **staleRoot 609 → 3894**
            (sixfold). Obvious in hindsight: if you root the search AHEAD of the player, then
            by construction the first emitted node will be about two blocks from where
            the bot is standing AT THE MOMENT OF EMISSION — exactly under the rejection threshold. The race isn't
            eliminated, it's guaranteed. Option closed.
        (b) make the search fast enough that the race never arises;
        (c) teach the executor to RE-SIMULATE the tail from the player's actual state —
            then a stale root stops being a problem in principle.
      ⛔ WHAT NOT TO DO: trimming the array and handing off the tail — measured worse (nav 10/12, freezes
      on flat ground), because the executor plays back RECORDED INPUTS, not points.

### The deal: take baritone's BEST, keep tungsten's BEST, kill neither

Baritone gives us two things it is genuinely better at: **building/breaking** and **SPEED**.
Tungsten gives one thing baritone cannot do at all: a **real physics simulation** of the player
body. Neither engine is being replaced. What was wrong is that each was being asked to do the
other's job.

| capability | owner | why |
|---|---|---|
| place / break as part of movement | **ported baritone `Movement`** (`tungsten/.../path/movements/`) | it owns the whole step: keys, aim, real crosshair click. tungsten's version split walking from placing and failed at a different seam every time |
| route planning, short and instant | **block-space BFS/A\*** (`FastPlanner`), baritone-shaped | this is HOW baritone is fast: block cells, not simulated bodies |
| swim / dive / enter+exit water / ladder / slime bounce | **physics engine** (`path/PathFinder`, `Node.getChildren`, `path/specialMoves/`) | it simulates the real body; nothing else can hold a heading in water or ride a bounce |
| hard parkour no block route can reach | **physics engine**, engaged LAST | only when there are no blocks and no way round |

**The physics engine is not to be deleted, weakened or bypassed.** It lives in
`tungsten/src/main/java/kaptainwutax/tungsten/path/PathFinder.java`, `path/Node.java`
(`getChildren` = move generation) and `path/specialMoves/` — 13 moves: `SwimmingMove`,
`DivingMove`, `EnterWaterAndSwimMove`, `ExitWaterMove`, `ClimbALadderMove`, `JumpToLadderMove`,
`SlimeBounceMove`, `LongJump`, `CornerJump`, `SprintJumpMove`, `TurnACornerMove`, `RunToNode`,
`WalkToNode` — driven through `PathInput`/`Agent`. Any pass touching these must say why.

### AC-1 - SPEED IS A FEATURE, AND WE ARE CURRENTLY FAILING IT

**The symptom, in the user's words: while the enemy runs away we recompute the whole route and
end up 100+ blocks behind the target. That is unacceptable.**

- [ ] **AC-1.1 Time to first step.** From "goal set" to "a movement key is pressed": single-digit
      milliseconds for a short route, not a planning budget. The search can already do this -
      measured 202 nodes in 1.7 ms once its own logging left the inner loop - so the budget is no
      longer the constraint, the pipeline is.
- [ ] **AC-1.2 Never recompute from scratch while moving.** A moving target is tracked by
      EXTENDING the plan, not replanning it. A full mid-chase replan is a defect, not a tuning
      parameter.
- [ ] **AC-1.3 Chase gate.** Against a target moving at sprint speed the bot stays within a few
      blocks and closes. "100+ blocks behind" is the current value and the number that must move.
- [ ] **AC-1.4 Run first, refine while running.** Start running the exact block route
      IMMEDIATELY. While running, compute the physics route FROM A FUTURE NODE and switch to it
      at that node ONLY if it came back faster in time. Never stand still waiting for a better
      idea.
- [ ] **AC-1.5 Minimal physics pass, instantly.** Baritone has no physics at all; we do. A simple
      route over the block nodes gets a MINIMAL physics check straight away - enough to know it is
      walkable, not a full simulation. The full search stays for the hard cases.

### AC-2 - ENGAGEMENT ORDER (what runs when)

- [ ] **AC-2.1** Block route first, always. It is the fast one.
- [ ] **AC-2.2** A step needing a block placed or broken goes to the ported baritone movement.
- [ ] **AC-2.3** Physics is engaged LAST: when the block route genuinely cannot reach - nothing in
      the pocket, no way round - then try the hard parkour move.
- [ ] **AC-2.4** Dispatch BY MOVE KIND, not by one `viaJump` flag. A waypoint that PLACES is not
      "physics": measured, `placeAcross` flags its planks `viaJump` and the plan is then handed to
      the one engine that has no place move at all.

### AC-3 - SIDE TASK: teach the physics side to PLACE

- [ ] **AC-3.1 Parkour-place.** Placing is fast, so it should be available to the physics side
      too: a block under yourself mid-jump when that is quicker than going round. After AC-1/AC-2.

### The two porting rules (user, 2026-07-30)

**RULE 1 - TAKE IT WHOLE, ADAPT LATER.** The BFS routing logic for placing and breaking comes over
from baritone ENTIRELY, verbatim, including parts that look redundant. Only once it WORKS on the
stand do we adapt it to tungsten's shape. Adapting during the port is what produced eight failed
passes on one course: a forged hit result instead of the real ray trace, `WALK * 2.5` instead of
the real `SNEAK_ONE_BLOCK_COST = 15.385`, a jump priced at 11.13 instead of 3.163, and a comment
claiming "the camera is cosmetic here".

**RULE 2 - ALWAYS RE-CHECK BOTH SIDES BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING.** Before adding any mechanism, open
baritone's version AND tungsten's own. Two questions, answered with `file:line`: *does this already
exist?* and *did we already hit this bug?* Then REUSE it. The cost of skipping this is on record:
an audit found **58 re-derived / 40 missing** behaviours (`docs/BARITONE-PORT.md`), and a whole
session went into rediscovering that the search burns its budget writing chat from the inner loop -
which this very file already carried as **C4.4**. See `docs/CHECKLIST.md` section 1b.

  `BlockNode.getNodesIn3DCircule(8, ...)` (`:356,412-468`) builds rings of radius `d=8` around the
  node for every height level `py`, on EVERY node expansion. For an ordinary (not `generateDeep`,

  (`:428`, `yMax=2` non-slime branch `:423`) — 6 values of `py`. Each `py` builds 1
  central node plus a ring `id=1..localD` (`localD = d+1 = 9`, `:437`) with `4*id` nodes per
  ring (`:446`) — total per `py`: `1 + 4*(1+2+...+9) = 1 + 4*45 = 181` nodes. Over 6 values of
  `py`: `6 * 181 = 1086` — THE NUMBER MATCHES EXACTLY, not an estimate, a direct recomputation of the code's formula.

  and bails constantly on a slope (`cooldown=78`, `wasStoppedByBail`), and physics doesn't solve that same
  leg either. This is exactly what `chase_terrain` is about, and it's work on the walker, not another
  patch in the chase.
  BOTTOM LINE FOR THE ITEM AFTER A DAY: the stand now measures the chase (view-distance), THREE real
  defects fixed (armed path; walker watchdog declared and never called; an unbounded target for
  physics), SEVEN hypotheses killed by measurement and listed above, and the task went from "the bot lags 100+
  blocks behind" to a named capability: TEACH THE WALKER TO WALK OVER TERRAIN.
  Meanwhile the machine came alive: `planCalls` grows, the bot moves between windows, `gap min` 34 → 29.
  A WATCHDOG THRESHOLD EXPERIMENT (single-parameter, 2026-08-01): `WALKER_STUCK_TICKS` 30 → 80 ticks.
  Rationale: 30 ticks is 1.5 s, and the constant NEVER worked (declared and never read), meaning
  its value was never validated; on a slope, one and a half seconds without HORIZONTAL
  movement is normal. Measured: `freezes` 14 → 12, `gap last` 111 → 109. Direction correct, magnitude
  WITHIN NOISE. The value 80 was kept (better justified than the untested 30), but IT DOESN'T FIX
  THE COURSE — and this confirms the main conclusion: the threshold is beside the point, the WALKER GENUINELY DOESN'T MOVE THE BODY.
  The walker's own log: `Walker: BFS 82` EIGHTY times and `BFS 76` SEVENTY-ONE — it receives
  82 waypoints and restarts with them again and again, making no progress.

      `if (!liveMode && TungstenModDataContainer.isExecutorRunning()) { stop(); return; }`
  THE WALKER STOPS ITSELF the moment the executor is running. In the chase, `startFind` launches the
  physical search; it returns a route; the executor kicks in — and the walker DROPS the block route.
  The executor plays back a physics path that never gets the bot to the runner, everything dies,

  DONE: the walker got an "this run is mine" mode (`startBFS(path, ownsMovement)`) — exactly the

  executor no longer switches off its route. nav 12/12, zero gate failures — navigation isn't
  affected (the gate is shared, so it was checked separately).

  apparently DOES describe the remainder after all — but now it can be verified ON A CLEAN STAND, where nobody
  switches it off.
  BOTTOM LINE FOR THE ITEM: five fixes in a day, THREE shifted the state (armed path; walker watchdog
  declared and never called; preemption), TWO didn't move the number (the leg for physics; watchdog

  READ TO THE END (`tickBFS`), and the remainder is named IN THE CODE ITSELF, not by me:
      "ADVANCE ON OCCUPANCY — CORRECT, BUT IT CANNOT LAND ALONE… Both halves have to land
       together, inside one movement, which is UNIT 2 of docs/BARITONE-PORT-SPEC.md."
  So `BlockPathWalker` is a HAND-WRITTEN APPROXIMATION, and the repository itself records that the correct

- [x] **C5.26 (2026-08-02) BOW: LEAD DIDN'T ACCOUNT FOR LATENCY. `ranged_moving` GREEN
  (1/6 → 2/6, gate ≥2).** Ballistics had nothing to do with it: an independent audit re-simulated
  the solver against vanilla arrow physics — a hit within 0.13 block all the way out to 40
  blocks, while the log of the failed run showed SIX clean releases with a 3-block lead at 10
  ticks of flight (the correct speed for a sprinting player). Five still missed, and ALL of them
  were behind the target. Two delays stack, both in the same direction:
  (a) the solve uses the CLIENT-INTERPOLATED position — a remote player moves via packets
  through a three-step lerp, whose settled lag is exactly three ticks of speed (this
  same model is already described in the repo where it explains why `getVelocity()` on a walking
  remote player is ~0); (b) the release happens 1-2 ticks after the solve, because releasing the
  key is only processed on the next `handleInputEvents()`.
  At a distance of 25 blocks with a ±0.6 window: without accounting for it — 0.38 behind at zero ticks and 1.30 at
  three; with `flight + 4` — +0.08, i.e. dead center, and the hit holds at 2, 3, and 4 ticks,
  so this is a constant, not a knob.
  ⛔ THE STAND WAS ALSO FIXED ALONG THE WAY: attribution of ranged hits checked the distance AT THE MOMENT
  HP loss was recorded, while one sampling iteration costs ~7.5 s. Measured in `allround`:
  t=1.0 dist=25.6 hp=20.0 → t=8.4 dist=2.2 hp=10.0 on a flat field with ZERO melee hits —
  those 10 HP could only have come from an arrow, and checking against 2.2 discarded it. The ranged
  test now takes the LARGEST discrepancy over the interval.

- [x] **C5.25 (2026-08-02) WATER IS A MOVE, NOT A TOWER: `MovementSwim`. THE COURSE IS FULLY GREEN.**
  `FastPlanner` always treated water as part of the route: inside water it expands ALL SIX
  directions, including `(0,+1,0)` surface and `(0,-1,0)` dive, and scores them as strokes.
  The executor had no class for this, so such edges fell to whichever LAND
  predicate happened to match the geometry — and a vertical edge matches `isPillarEdge`.
  A bot swimming in a lake would get ordered to build a tower under itself to climb out.
  Measured, then checked against the world: 34 fallbacks in one run, ALL of them —
  `MovementPillar (-177,62,290)->(-177,63,290)`, and rcon confirms the source is `minecraft:water`
  and the target is air above it. This is SURFACING, executed as a pillar.
  `MovementSwim` takes any edge with liquid on either end, AHEAD OF all
  land predicates. No mechanics needed: vanilla swims for you — aim, hold forward,
  and the base `update()` already presses JUMP while the feet are in liquid and the body is below
  `dest.y + 0.6` (that's exactly "swim across" and "surface"); diving is simply NOT pressing it. Arrival is
  measured by distance, not by cell, because a swimmer sways between two.
  RESULT: the failure breakdown is EMPTY (used to be 34), and the verdict is green ACROSS THE BOARD —
  on land, the target ran 517 blocks, caught it, killed it, 0 deaths, 0 freezes, no command errors.
  nav 12/12, gate failures 0.

- [x] **C5.24 (2026-08-02) ⛔ LAST SOURCE OF FREEZES — AN ATTEMPT TO BREAK OUT WATER.
  `chase_terrain` GREEN: 0 freezes TWO RUNS IN A ROW, nav 12/12.**
  `Movement.prepared()` aims at every cell in `positionsToBreak` where `canWalkThrough` is false,
  and holds `CLICK_LEFT` until the block disappears. Current water fails `canWalkThrough` →
  it ends up there → water cannot be broken → `prepared()` will NEVER return true, and since
  `Movement.updateState` returns PREPPING BEFORE the subclass's own logic, the step never
  arrives and never fails either. It just sits until the `cost+100` timeout — 8 seconds each time.
  Diagnosis, not a guess: the timeout log named THE SAME flat step
  `(-157,60,288)->(-156,60,288)` every time, and rcon on the live world answered that the feet, the head, and
  the target cell were all `minecraft:water`.
  MEASUREMENT (stand fixed, the target actually runs):
      run1 freezes=0 runner_path=512.7 mqStarted=4 mqSteps=122 mqTimeout=0
      run2 freezes=0 runner_path=524.0 mqStarted=7 mqSteps=242 mqTimeout=0
      nav  12/12, gate failures 0 (including nav_water)
  30-34 executed steps per chain, versus 0.11 at the start of the session.
  ⚠️ OPEN: WHETHER the route should go through water at all is a PLANNER question. It reasons
  by geometry (`PlayerFit`), the moves by baritone predicates, and on water they disagree. The executor
  simply no longer spends eight seconds on an impossible action.

- [~] **C5.20 (2026-08-02) THE PORTED-MOVE QUEUE FINALLY DRIVES THE CHASE — a chain of five
  defects, each found by MEASUREMENT, not reasoning.**
  Starting state: `MovementQueue.start()` had EXACTLY ONE caller
  (`FastNavigator:373`, and only for the leg that PLACES blocks). Any ordinary walking — in both
  nav and the chase — went through the hand-written `BlockPathWalker`; the ported moves took no
  part in movement. Order in which the causes were uncovered (`mq*` counters in `placeStats`):
  1. **The lever didn't exist** (C5.19) — four A/Bs were comparing the build against itself.
     Fixed: `tungstenSetting()` + `run_suite --pin` with a mandatory read-back check.
  2. **Prep cannot fail, only be sat through.** `Movement.updateState`, when
     `!prepared()`, returns PREPPING and exits BEFORE checking arrival → a move sat for
     `cost+100` ticks. Measured: `mqTimeout=13` of 15 chains, five of six — `MovementAscend`,
     **one of them while standing exactly in the target cell**. A start-of-chain check was introduced.
  3. **`MovementPillar` had nobody dispatching to it**, and `isSupportedEdge` never let an
     upward step through at all → it BROKE THE PREFIX. 52 of 107 failures were `MovementFallback (0,88,-283)
     ->(0,89,-283)`, meaning steering instead of a pillar. Plus `MovementPillar` couldn't switch
     slots (its neighbors get that for free via `attemptToPlaceABlock`).
  4. **`VoidGuard` was stealing the queue's keys.** It's called AFTER `MovementQueue.tick` and wasn't
     gated by a tick-ownership flag: it read the just-pressed `MOVE_FORWARD`, measured
     `fallHeight 4` against a hardcoded limit of 3, and turned on SNEAK — pinning the body to the edge.
     It only fired on falls ≥3 (height counted from the original feet = drop+1), so
     nobody saw it apart from `MovementFall`: 25 timeouts out of 26 chains, at 161 ticks each.
  5. **Water was throwing out the whole route.** Current water fails `canWalkThrough` →
     lands in `toBreak` → `BreakRules` forbids breaking liquid → the check considered the step
     impossible. ALL truncations were `minecraft:water`, 68 per run, "`cut to 0/40`".
  MEASURED RESULT (stand fixed, lever verified): `mqStarted=134 mqSteps=159 mqRefused=0
  mqTimeout=8`, freezes 8 and 4 versus 15 and 0 for the walker. NO VERDICT YET — alternating
  pairs are needed, they're underway. The remaining failures and timeouts are `MovementTraverse`.

- [x] **C5.21 CLOSED (2026-08-02, attempt 3). THE BLOCK-SPACE SEARCH IS AN A* AGAIN.
      nav 12/12, gate failures 0; pvp 9/12 — no regression.**
  All six defects landed together: a relaxation guard with the REAL edge cost (used to be
  `child.cost + 1` — the wrong recipient and a literal instead of the move cost, and since every child
  is freshly allocated, `child.cost` was always 0, meaning `f = h + 1` — a greedy search, and every
  cost in `ActionCosts`/`SmartMoves` was dead), `cost = 0` at the start, a declared
  `failureTimeoutTime`, a threshold of 0.01 instead of -500, an honest heuristic with its seeding, removed
  extraneous `continue` and `&& !failing`.
  ⛔ WHY ATTEMPT 2 GAVE 8/12 — NOT THE HEURISTIC. `setCurrentPath` was calling
  `initializeBestHeuristics` and THROWING AWAY THE RETURN VALUE: on re-rooting, a new open
  list and a new start were set, while the thresholds stayed from the PREVIOUS root.
  At -500 this was unnoticeable; at 0.01 the record is monotonic, no child of the new root
  beats the old thresholds, `bestSoFar` remains the start node (whose `parent == null`),
  `bestSoFar()` returns empty — and the bot emits ONE partial path, after which it stands until the
  20 s ceiling. Three courses at once — that was it.

  re-discovered from scratch a second time.
  THE DEFECT, per `TriggerBot.java`'s own embedded multi-day investigation (2026-08-12/13,
  already fully carried out, not this session's work): a swing matures (cooldown ready) while the
  target is out of `TriggerBot.REACH` in roughly half of all ready ticks on `allround`
  (readyFar/readyNear near 50/50 across six runs). Chased through five refuted hypotheses in
  order — closing speed, `ProjectileDodge` stealing the legs, keys not reaching the game, raw
  forward-press absence — before landing on the actual cause: `CombatController`'s own
  circle-strafe holds a diagonal (forward + a strafe key) through 18-78% of the wasted ticks,
  and a 45-degree diagonal only points ~70% of sprint speed at the target — enough that a
  5.6 b/s sprinting bot closes at ~3.9 against a target retreating at ~5, i.e. it LOSES ground
  while honestly holding sprint. Confirmed independently in `CombatController.java` too (its own
  comment above `strafeFarTicks`/`strafeNearTicks`, dated the next day, closes the same question
  from that side).
  THE FIX: `TungstenConfig.combatApproachNoOrbit` (`TungstenConfig.java:4342`, default `false`)
  already exists and is already wired into `CombatController.java:1194` — written specifically to
  make the circle-strafe yield while a swing is ready and the target is out of reach, per
  `TriggerBot.java`'s own closing note ("written and gated behind its own flag pending outcome
  validation, not shipped as of this reading"). Nothing since suggests it was ever actually run.
  NOT MEASURED, NOT FIXED THIS SESSION (C8.1) — this entry exists purely so the A/B this defect
  has been waiting on since 2026-08-13 is visible to whoever next has a stand, instead of sitting
  only in a source-file comment nobody greps the register for.

    (`PathFinder.java:395-456`) does `thread = new Thread(() -> { ... search(...) ... });
    thread.start(); return true;` — the read of `TungstenConfig.get().searchTimeoutMs`
    (`:414,500`) and of `minDistPath` (`:510` and again at `:1078`, deep inside the search's
    own node-selection loop) all happen INSIDE that background thread, at some point AFTER
    `thread.start()` returns control to the caller with no ordering guarantee. So the
    obvious-looking fix — save the old value, call `pf.find(...)`, restore the old value right
    after — is a genuine RACE: the search thread might not have reached its own read yet when
    the restore runs on the calling thread, in which case the search silently gets the ORIGINAL
    (non-fallback) tuning instead of the one this method exists to apply, defeating the whole
    point of `applyFallbackTuning` unpredictably, run to run. This is exactly why the comment
    already sitting in the code calls for "per-call search parameters" rather than a
    save/restore pair — the values need to be captured into the search's own closure BEFORE
    the thread starts, not stored in a shared mutable field read on a timeline the caller does
    not control.
  * **NOT ATTEMPTED THIS PASS.** The real fix touches `PathFinder.find()`'s signature (or adds
    an overload) and threads the override values through `search()` down to at least two call
    sites (`:500`, `:1078`, and possibly more not yet traced past that point) — a genuine,
    moderate `PathFinder` API change to the mod's core physics search, called from
    `FastNavigator`, `GotoCommand`, `PathExecutor`, `BlockPlaceHelper` and `TungstenHelper`
    itself. I have no compiler and no live stand with a build in this session to verify a
    change to the search engine everything else in the mod depends on, and a wrong change here
    risks being worse than the leak it fixes. Left for whoever has both.
  * ⛔ ADDED 2026-09-04, SECOND PASS — full call-graph trace of `minDistPath`, not just its
    two direct readers, to check whether the scope above was actually the whole picture. It is
    not; the scope is LARGER than "two call sites", confirming (not narrowing) the conclusion
    above. Traced by grep, not guessed: `minDistPath` field decl `PathFinder.java:105`, read at
    `:510` (inside `search()`) and `:1078` (inside `bestSoFar(boolean, int, Node, Vec3d)`).
    `bestSoFar()` itself has exactly two callers: `handleTimeout()` (`:1924`) and
    `setCurrentPath()` (`:1943`). `handleTimeout()` is a private instance method with exactly
    ONE caller, `:845`, inside `search()`'s own main loop — so that half of the graph stays
    inside the one async search thread, as already described above. `setCurrentPath()`,
    however, is a private STATIC method with AT LEAST EIGHT call sites spread across the file:
    lines 722, 765, 992, 1049, 1934, 2460, 2467 (commented out), 2493 — not confined to
    `search()`'s call chain at all. So a save/restore fix around a single `pf.find(...)` call
    would still race not just against the search thread's own two reads, but against every one
    of those eight `setCurrentPath()` call sites too, several of which are plainly reachable
    from outside the search thread (a path being accepted/replaced as it arrives). This does
    not open a narrower fix; it rules one out. The API-change conclusion above stands, now on
    firmer evidence — still not attempted, still needs a build to verify.

### G-1.8 — the planner laid bridges while holding ZERO blocks (fixed), next up — going around the pond

`FastPlanner.placeBudget` is a static with a starting value of `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, and
EXACTLY ONE caller set it, `FastNavigator:443`. The playthrough runs through
`CustomBaritoneGoalTask`, i.e. bypassing it — meaning the budget stayed infinite, and
the planner laid a bridge and a pillar with an empty inventory. The hazard was noted right in
a comment at `FastPlanner:900` ("placeBudget does not cover it: it is MAX_VALUE until a
caller sets it"), but never closed.

Measured BEFORE: the bot stood at the pond's edge, the planner asked for a one-block bridge, the executor
answered "Bridge place aborted (no block in hand)" every tick — `placeCalled=1219` with
`placeDeferred=0` and `placeInRange=0` (it never even got as far as checking the distance).

Fixed: the budget is now taken from `countPlaceable` at the start of EVERY planning pass, instead of
being inherited from someone else's static. Measured AFTER: `called=1219 -> 0`. nav: **11/12, 0
gate failures**, `nav_bridge` and `nav_break` — both PASS (the only INVALID = the host starving).

⛔ NEXT BLOCKER: now that a bridge is honestly unavailable, the planner is obligated to GO AROUND the pond —
and doesn't. `mqStarted=0`, the bot wobbles in place (y 62.1-63.1). The pass's question: what does
`FastPlanner` return for this goal with `placeBudget=0` — a route around it, an empty result,
or a partial one. Look at the plan's result, not the execution.

AN EXTRA MEASUREMENT for G-1.8 (right after the budget fix): the client log for the run has NOT A SINGLE
`FastPlanner:` line — only `WALKMODE off=9298 bfs=102 direct=0`, with the `off` counter
climbing. So once a bridge honestly became unavailable, the planner isn't called AT ALL
for this goal, rather than "being called and returning a detour". So the search should be not in
`FastPlanner`, but ABOVE it — in whatever decides to call it: `WALKMODE off` = the walker mode
is disabled, `bfs=102` = the cheap grid BFS ran 102 times, `direct=0`.

### G-1.16 — FOUND AND FIXED: the bot wasn't walking, it was re-planning — a search every two ticks

The counter on the near branch's outcome gave the answer immediately: `pdNearFind` = **2460 and 2707 per run**.

FOUR blocks away. Not a single search survived long enough for its path to be walked; the bot stood still until
the 5-second reset fired (`pdStallReset` 14 and 17).

The cause is structural: within a 4-block radius the block route doesn't work at all (the branch is gated behind
`distToGoal > 4.0`), and the bot is in this radius **98% of the time** (`pdNear` ~5000 out of ~5100). So
the whole game is being driven by the physics executor — and it was restarting every tick whenever it wasn't
busy.

Fixed with a 600ms delay on re-planning (the same technique adopted for block placement, #31). Measured:

|---|---|---|
| searches per run | 2460-2707 | **207-384** |
| nav resets | 14-17 | **6-12** |
| summary | 0/2 | **2/3, threshold cleared** |
| nav | 12/12 | **12/12, 0 failures** |

CAVEAT: the summary's variance is high (from 0/3 to 2/3 over the evening), so "2/3" alone is not
proof. The proof is the mechanism's own counters: a tenfold drop in the number of searches
cannot be noise. Next pass: repeat the summary over 5 runs for a stable rate,
and dig into the remaining 6-12 resets.

### G-1.18 — the mechanism behind the remaining failures: the path RUNS OUT without arriving, and that isn't counted as a failure

`PathExecutor.isRunning()` (PathExecutor.java:256) returns
`path != null && !armed && tick <= path.size()`. Meaning once the path is EXHAUSTED
(`tick > path.size()`), the executor declares itself NOT busy, while the `path` itself is left in place —
nobody checks whether the bot actually ARRIVED. The near branch of `CustomBaritoneGoalTask` sees
`!busy` and orders a new search. The circle closes.

This is exactly what the numbers show: in the failed run, `pdNearBusy=1455` and
`pdNearFind=385` against `304/62` in the best one — the executor ends up
free five times as often, meaning it finishes the path in vain five times as often.

⛔ NEXT PASS'S TASK (a core fix, not a patch): a path that ran out without reaching the goal
must be counted as a FAILURE and say so, instead of silently freeing the executor.
THE SAME WORKING ORDER THAT HAS PAID OFF: first a COUNTER on path outcomes (arrived /
ran out without arriving / stopped), one summary run — and only then the fix.
Six times this session the counter gave the answer on the first run; both "guessed"
fixes had to be rolled back.

2. find the entry whose result matches `target.getOutputItem()`;
3. pass its `id()` to `clickRecipe(syncId, NetworkRecipeId, boolean)`.

guess at intermediate APIs.

### G-1.47 — ⭐⭐⭐ FOUND BY READING: `isPlayerInventoryOpen()` IS ALWAYS TRUE

```java
private static boolean isScreenOpenInner(Predicate<ScreenHandler> p) {
    return p.test(player.currentScreenHandler);      // <- HANDLER, not screen
}
public static boolean isPlayerInventoryOpen() {
    return isScreenOpenInner(sh -> sh instanceof PlayerScreenHandler);
}
```

`PlayerScreenHandler` is the DEFAULT handler: it stays as `currentScreenHandler` when no screen
at all is open. So `isPlayerInventoryOpen()` returns **true ALWAYS**.

THIS EXPLAINS EVERYTHING THAT WAS MEASURED: `cgInv` = every tick, `cgNoScreen` = 0 always, and
the crafting task, believing the screen is open, NEVER OPENS IT — and the server drops the craft
request because the screen is actually closed. Hence `cgOutReady=0` with a healthy book and a
packet that leaves.

⛔ FIX (CORE, but CAREFUL): check the REAL screen —
`MinecraftClient.getInstance().currentScreen instanceof InventoryScreen` — not the handler.
RISK: `isPlayerInventoryOpen()` is used in MANY places (see the count in the commit), and the
"always true" behavior may have become an implicit crutch for other code. So:
1. first add a SEPARATE, honest method (e.g. `isPlayerInventoryScreenOpen()`) and
   apply IT ONLY in the crafting task;
2. measure with a summary (`--repeat 3 --rung crafting`) + nav 12/12;
3. only then decide whether to fix `isPlayerInventoryOpen()` itself globally.
DO NOT change the shared helper in one sweep — this is exactly the case where a "correct" fix
can break a dozen places at once.

### G-1.54 — ⭐ FOUND THE SLOT BLACKLIST. And my counter was sitting IN THE WRONG PLACE

`SlotHandler.clickWindowSlot` has a SECOND, undocumented bail-out:

```java
BlacklistKey blKey = new BlacklistKey(syncId, windowSlot);
Long blExpiry = _slotBlacklist.get(blKey);
if (blExpiry != null && System.currentTimeMillis() < blExpiry) return;   // silently
```

Next to it is a snapshot of the slot's state and `_pendingSlotActions` for "detecting a server
cancel". So the mechanism is: clicked the slot -> server cancelled it -> slot goes on the
BLACKLIST -> subsequent clicks are SILENTLY DROPPED.

THIS EXPLAINS WHAT WAS MEASURED BEST OF ALL: the item is in the slot, the task clicks 2620 times,
`shIssued=1711` — but `shIssued` is incremented BEFORE this check, meaning part of the
"sent" clicks NEVER REACH `controller.clickSlot`.

⛔ MY OWN MISTAKE, NOTING IT DOWN: the `shIssued` counter sits IN THE WRONG SPOT — it counts
intent, not action. The same lesson as with `cgOutReady` (a counter on a cold path): PLACE THE
COUNTER RIGHT AGAINST THE ACTION it's supposed to be measuring.

NEXT PASS:

2. add a counter for bail-outs by the blacklist and for a slot ENTERING the blacklist;
3. if confirmed — figure out WHY the server cancels the click on the crafting output slot
   (and whether the "cancel detection" itself is false for the output slot, where the stack
   NATURALLY changes after a click — the "before" snapshot and the "after" comparison are bound
   to differ there!).
   ⚠ THE LAST POINT IS A STRONG SUSPICION: for the crafting OUTPUT slot, the stack changing after
   a click is NORMAL, and the detector apparently reads this as a server cancel and bans the slot.

### G-1.55 — ⭐⭐⭐ MECHANISM FOUND BY READING: the cancel detector FALSE-TRIGGERS on the output slot

`SlotHandler.onServerSlotUpdate` bans a slot when the server state EQUALS the state BEFORE
the click:

```java
if (... && ItemStack.areEqual(serverStack, action.before())) { ...blacklist... }
```

For a regular slot this is correct: unchanged after the click = server rolled it back.
BUT FOR THE CRAFTING OUTPUT SLOT, a successful collect LOOKS THE SAME: took 4 planks -> a log
is still left in the grid -> the slot REFILLS with 4 planks again -> `serverStack` EQUALS
`before` bit for bit. A successful craft is indistinguishable from a cancel.

And the blacklist is ESCALATING: 4s -> 30s -> **600s**. So after THREE successful crafts the
output slot gets locked for TEN MINUTES, and every further click is silently dropped.
This fully explains it: the item is in the slot (`ciReceive` 98%), the task clicks thousands of
times, the item doesn't leave.

⛔ FIX (core): exclude crafting OUTPUT slots from cancel detection — a collected-and-refilled
output is NOT a cancel. Candidate conditions: `windowSlot == 0` for `PlayerScreenHandler`, and
`CraftingTableSlot.OUTPUT_SLOT` for `CraftingScreenHandler`; cleaner — check that the slot IS a
`CraftingResultSlot`.
CHECK: summary `--repeat 3 --rung crafting` + nav 12/12, and a counter for entering the
blacklist (should hit zero for the output slot).

STATUS OF THE CONCLUSION: obtained by READING, NOT yet confirmed by measurement. Confirmation
is the first thing in the next pass: a counter for "slot blacklisted" with the slot number. If
the output slot is among them — the mechanism is proven.

### G-1.82 — ⭐⭐⭐ CAUSE OF THE DISCONNECT: THE MOD DISCONNECTS ITSELF ON DEATH AND NEVER COMES BACK

Server: `tester1 lost connection: Disconnected` — a CLEAN, client-initiated departure, not a
timeout and not a kick.

Source found in `GameMenuTaskChain`:
- `_innerDisconnect(client)` calls `client.world.disconnect()` and
  `client.disconnect(new DisconnectedScreen(..., Text.of("DEATH")))` — i.e. it disconnects
  ON DEATH, by design: the mod reconnects in order to respawn;
- next `_reconnecting = true` and `setScreen(new MultiplayerScreen(new TitleScreen()))`.

BUT THE RECONNECT ISN'T COMPLETED: the client stays on the title screen (in the log — Realms
authorization attempts, which is the title screen) until the end of the run. This fits with the
bot connecting via a DIRECT ADDRESS (`py4j connect ip=gamer-server`), while the recovery
mechanism relies on `_prevServerEntry` / a server list, which doesn't exist for a direct
connection.

FULL CHAIN, FROM SYMPTOM TO ROOT (every link measured):
the bot dies -> the mod DISCONNECTS the client (intentional) -> reconnecting fails for a direct
connection -> client stuck on the title screen -> `inGame=False` until the end of the run ->
polling returns zeros -> "empty inventory", "items are lost", "18 minutes = one rung",
"counters are zero", "the bench crashes". ALL OF THIS IS THE SAME THING.

⛔ FIX FOR THE NEXT PASS (core, not the bench): save the DIRECT connection address and restore
the session using it, not only via `_prevServerEntry`. Check: a long run (15+ min) with no
`inGame=False` in the polls + a summary on the `wood tools` rung.
AS A TEMPORARY MEASURE the bench can reconnect on its own (this is NOT a substitute for the
fix, just a tool to measure the upper rungs while the fix isn't done yet).

### G-1.83 — the recovery mechanism read IN FULL; do the fix with a fresh head

`GameMenuTaskChain.onTickPost` (lines 356-382) can reconnect:
- waits for the screen to initialize (`if (screen.children().isEmpty()) return;` — otherwise the
  client crashes on 1.21.11);
- takes `_prevServerEntry` (it IS FILLED every tick in-game from `getCurrentServerEntry()`,
  line 225 — meaning it's ALSO filled on a direct connection; my guess from G-1.82 about an
  "empty server list" is NOT CONFIRMED);
- calls `ConnectScreenVer.connect(...)` inside a try/catch with a retry.

SO THE MECHANISM EXISTS AND LOOKS CORRECT. What's observed instead is the TITLE screen (Realms
authorization attempts in the log) and `inGame=False` until the end of the run. So the
reconnect branch NEVER GETS REACHED: on death the client leaves via `DisconnectedScreen`
(`Text.of("DEATH")`), and it looks like `_reconnecting` isn't set on this path, or the screen
turns out to be the wrong one for the guard.

⛔ NEXT PASS (a core fix, do it WITH A FRESH HEAD — this is a state machine with ~6 flags, and
a mistake here is costly):
1. MEASURE FIRST, as always: counters on `_needDisconnect`, `_reconnecting`,
   `reconnectAttemps`, and on the guard `screen.children().isEmpty()` — which of them doesn't
   fire;
2. then ONE fix: guarantee that the death path sets `_reconnecting` and brings the client to a
   screen the guard lets through;
3. verification: a long run with no `inGame=False` + a summary on `wood tools`.

HONESTLY: my guess from G-1.82 ("doesn't work because of the direct connection, empty server
list") was NOT CONFIRMED by reading — `_prevServerEntry` is filled from the current connection
regardless of method. My eleventh hypothesis this session, the tenth wrong one. The cause is
somewhere else in the same state machine.

### G-1.84 — ⛔ DISPROVED: `GameMenuTaskChain` does NOT disconnect the client. All its steps = 0

Counters on EVERY step of the "death -> disconnect -> reconnect" path:

    gmDisc=0  gmRecSet=0  gmGuard=0  gmConn=0

while in this same run the bot was `inGame=False` most of the time.

SO THE G-1.82 CONCLUSION IS WRONG: `_innerDisconnect` was NEVER called, `_reconnecting` was
never set, the guard never fired, `connect` was never called. The disconnect comes from
SOMEWHERE ELSE. (The counters are static and read from the live client process sitting on the
title screen — meaning the zeros are trustworthy, not "didn't get read in time".)

My eleventh and twelfth hypotheses this session, both wrong. Measurement was right again, and
"found a plausible spot in the code" was not. IMPORTANT LESSON: finding a mechanism in the code
that COULD explain the symptom is NOT proof that it does explain it. A counter is needed RIGHT
AT THAT SPOT, not reasoning about how well it fits.

⛔ NEXT PASS: look for the REAL source of the disconnect:
1. a counter/log on `MixinClientPlayNetworkHandler.onDisconnect` (or equivalent) — find the

2. check the py4j `connect` path (the bench calls it at the start; is it being called again?);

### G-1.89 — INSTRUMENT SLIP #9, AND IT'S A REPEAT: `head` cuts a run short

The measurement returned EMPTY output (0 lines). The cause isn't the bench: `... | grep ... | head -34`
closes the stream, and the run gets killed by SIGPIPE PARTWAY THROUGH. This is the exact same
mistake I already made this session (that time it was `head -12`), noted down, and repeated
anyway.

RULE FOR THE REGISTRY: NEVER put `head` at the end of a pipeline with a LIVE run. Output can
only be limited AFTER completion (read the file), or with a filter that doesn't truncate.

Tally of instrument issues this session: nine slips, one of them a repeat. This costs more than
any single fix — because of them I fixed working code three times and once lost several passes
chasing a nonexistent problem ("survival").

### G-1.92 — ⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE HANG EXPLAINED: THE "FLEE" GOAL DOESN'T TRANSLATE, AND THE BOT FREEZES

Counters from that exact run where the bot stood still for 4+ minutes:

    pdEnter=596   pdNoVec=368 (62%)   unknownGoal=GoalRunAwayFromHostiles
    mqStarted=5   mqSteps=38   mqTicks=589
    pdStuck=0     pdStallReset=0      exArrived=0  exRanOut=0

62% of navigation entries die at goal translation, and that goal is
**`GoalRunAwayFromHostiles`**. So the bot tries to FLEE, tungsten can't translate such a goal
(it has no point by definition), steps aside — and the legacy driver doesn't move it either.
Result: the bot freezes.

THIS IS THE EXACT SAME GAP FROM G-1.36 that I noted back then and SHELVED with the words
"doesn't interfere with mining". IT DOES INTERFERE — just not the way I thought: not by lacking
flight, but by COMPLETELY STOPPING the bot for the whole time the goal is active. Lesson:
"doesn't interfere" is also a hypothesis, and it also needs to be measured, not declared.

⛔ FIX FOR THE NEXT PASS (core): teach `goalToVec` to translate the flight goal INTO A POINT —
take the bot's position and back away from the nearest hostile entities by
`DANGER_KEEP_DISTANCE`. This is an honest translation: "flee" = "go to a point away from them",
and tungsten has something to reach a point with. Look at `RunAwayFromEntitiesTask` /
`GoalRunAwayFromHostiles` — where to take the entity list and distance from.
CHECK: `pdNoVec` should drop, positions in runs should stop freezing, time to the first log
should converge to the lower bound (22-70 s instead of 22-585).

   during a run (the bench does this itself on `StandDown`), and a saved pid goes stale — which
   is exactly what happened.

freeze): `RUNNER active=true | Chain: UserTaskChain, priority: 50.0` — the task runner is
ACTIVE and the user chain IS WINNING the tick. So it's not chain selection that freezes, but
something inside: the chain is chosen, but its task isn't progressing. This narrows the dump
search down to the `UserTaskChain.onTick -> ...` stack.

### G-1.110 — ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ ROOT OF THE HANG FOUND: `join()` IN THE CLIENT TICK, SHREDDER CODE

A dump taken with OUR OWN method (py4j) at exactly the moment caught by the watchdog:

    "Render thread" WAITING
        java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.join()
        at baritone.api.utils.BlockOptionalMeta$ServerLevelStub.holder(BlockOptionalMeta.java:306)
        at baritone.api.utils.BlockOptionalMeta.getDrops(BlockOptionalMeta.java:259)
        at baritone.api.utils.BlockOptionalMeta.drops(BlockOptionalMeta.java:226)
        at baritone.api.utils.BlockOptionalMeta.getStackHashes(BlockOptionalMeta.java:156)

THE RENDER THREAD (= THE CLIENT TICK) IS WAITING FOREVER ON `CompletableFuture.join()` inside
`BlockOptionalMeta$ServerLevelStub.holder` — while computing a block's DROP.

THIS IS NOT A DEADLOCK (my version from G-1.105 IS WRONG — the fourteenth hypothesis, the
thirteenth mistaken one). It's WAITING ON A FUTURE THAT NEVER COMPLETES, called synchronously
from the client tick. And the code lives in `shredder` (package `baritone.api.utils`), i.e. in
the very SAME module the project is replacing.

THIS EXPLAINS EVERYTHING: the mod tick freezes entirely (all counters to zero), there's no
exception (this is waiting, not a crash), the client stays in-game and "busy", the bot stands
still until the end of the run. And the intermittency: `getStackHashes` isn't called every tick,
only when working with specific blocks — hence "sometimes, sometimes not".

⛔ FIX FOR THE NEXT PASS: `ServerLevelStub.holder` in `shredder` MUST NOT block the client
thread. Options (in decreasing order of correctness):
1. don't call `join()` from the tick at all — return an empty/default result if the future isn't
   ready (`getNow(...)`), and compute the drop asynchronously;
2. cache the `getStackHashes`/`drops` result and compute it outside the tick;
3. at minimum — `join()` with a timeout, so the hang turns into degradation rather than death.
CHECK: the watchdog must catch zero `FROZEN` events over a summary of 3 runs.

`javap` on the new jar: **0 calls to `join`, 1 wait with a timeout**; (2) `deploy_jar.sh`
now calls `deploy/check_nested_fresh.py` and REFUSES to deploy if the module's jar is older than
its sources or the nested copy isn't byte-for-byte equal to the built one. The guard is TESTED
on a failure (`touch` a source -> refusal, exit=1), not just on green — this is the internal

### G-1.117 — the ray obstruction isn't just leaves; and the ladder was lying RED

THE FREEZE SNAPSHOT (new evidence on a frozen position) gave an exit distribution:

    pdEnter=721  ->  pdNear=487 (68%), pdNearBusy=135, pdWalking=0

    blockedBy=minecraft:dark_oak_log,  rayOther=502  vs  rayLeaves=10

So the bot was standing right next to an oak and aiming at a log blocked by a NEIGHBORING LOG of
the same canopy — while `RotationHelper` only remembered the obstruction position FOR LEAVES,
zeroing it out for anything else. The obstruction-clearing existed, but had nothing to clear:
1525 ticks, zero blocks broken.

FIX (core, not a patch): the obstruction position is now ALWAYS written (the kinds are still
counted separately), and the decision of "what may be cleared" belongs to the caller, who knows
the task. There are exactly three limiters and no more: unbreakable (hardness < 0), liquid, and
the block UNDER THE BOT'S OWN FEET (otherwise it digs itself in while staring at the tree).

MEASUREMENT: clearing started working (`leafCle+62` in a single interval where it used to be
zero), the best run — craft 21.8s → workbench 65.8s → wood tools 65.8s → **STONE tools 88.1s**.

⛔ AND RIGHT THERE — A FALSE RED. The summary declared that very best run `wood: NOT reached`,
FAIL: rungs are determined by what you're HOLDING, and by that point the log had already been
spent on planks, the table and tools. The ladder didn't know how to count "went DEEPER" as
"passed". This is the same family as the false greens cleaned up earlier (a check that can never
fail), just with the opposite sign. Fixed: any reached rung BELOW the required one credits the
required one. The logic is tested on 4 cases — credits deeper, credits an exact match, REFUSES
on empty, and REFUSES when the required rung is deeper than the one reached.

### G-1.119 — mob combat moved onto tungsten (user's question)

USER'S QUESTION: "did you make mob combat nice through our tungsten, or is it still the old
crap?" — the honest answer was: PvP is on tungsten, but MOBS stayed on the old code.
Now they're moved over.

WHERE EXACTLY. The analysis showed TWO different spots, and this matters:
- `MobDefenseChain.doForceField` — the "force field", called on EVERY priority-evaluation tick,
  even when the chain doesn't win the tick (in a snapshot: `mdCalls=3110` with all `mdRet`=0). It
  deliberately does NOT touch movement: the bot chops a tree and swats along the way. Routing
  `CombatController` here (it drives the keys) would mean taking the bot's legs away every time
  a mob is nearby. NOT TOUCHING IT.
- `AbstractKillEntityTask` — the place where the bot DELIBERATELY fights. This had a homegrown
  duel: cooldown-gated strikes, `GoJump`, shuffling near an edge. This is what got replaced.

WHAT WAS DONE:
1. inside strike range, combat is run by `CombatController.tick(player, target, world)` —
   aiming at a predicted position, holding distance, circular strafing, crit-jumps, breaking
   contact below half health (the same engine that raised duels 7/12 -> 9/12);
2. the approach is UNTOUCHED — altoclef's pathfinder still leads to the target;
3. aim is handed to a SINGLE owner: `smoothLook` now runs only outside strike range, otherwise
   there'd be two writers per tick fighting over the crosshair;
4. "no damage -> change angle -> mark unreachable" is switched from counting OUR swings to TIME
   SPENT IN STRIKE RANGE (4s) — otherwise, since the controller does the hitting, the swing
   counter would freeze at zero and the machinery would go blind;
5. the `kaTung` counter is exposed in the stats and reset between runs — so "does the new path
   work" is a NUMBER, not a belief.

⛔ IMPORTANT ABOUT THE MEASUREMENT: the PvP suite gave 7/12 against a 9/12 baseline — and this is
NOT about this fix. PvP courses run the `punk` command, i.e. tungsten's `PunkPlayerTask`, which
DOESN'T GO through the changed class. The fix is a provable no-op for them. Exactly the same trap
as the "regression" on the peaceful server: comparing scores without asking WHETHER the fix
could even affect this course. It needs checking where the bot actually fights mobs through the
kill task.

### G-1.120 — ⛔ THE BOT DOESN'T FIGHT MOBS. IT FLEES. (the G-1.119 fix never runs)

The tungsten combat hookup (G-1.119) is written and built, but VERIFICATION showed it DOESN'T
WORK — because control never reaches it. Chain of measurements:

1. The PvP suite — not suitable: courses run `punk` (`PunkPlayerTask`), the changed class isn't
   touched.
2. `@gamer` runs (3 of them) — `kaTung=0`: a bot chopping wood by day never enters melee.
3. A targeted probe (`deploy/runner/mob_fight_test.py`): spawn a zombie, issue `@test kill`.

THE PROBE FIRST LIED, and this is a mistake of the same class already caught before: the
zombie's aliveness was checked via `execute if entity ... run say ALIVE`, and rcon answers this
form with EMPTINESS — meaning every poll read "dead", and the three "3.7s fights" were the three
first polls. The form `execute if entity @e[type=zombie]` answers `Test passed. Count: N` — a
fact, not silence.

WITH AN HONEST PROBE: the zombie stands still for 34 seconds at FULL health 20.0, the bot loses
its own (17->14) and DOES NOT STRIKE BACK, `kaTung=0/0/0/0` — meaning `kaTaskTicks=0`, the combat
task never started at all.

CAUSE FOUND. Right after `@test kill`, what's running is:

    Mob Defense task chain | Main task: <NIGERUNDAYOO, SUMOOKEYY! distance=30.0, skeletons=true>

This is `RunAwayFromEntities`. The defense chain (priority 70) overrides the user chain (50) and
chooses FLIGHT — from a SINGLE zombie, while holding an iron sword and full health. The combat
task never gets a tick, and the entire tungsten dueling mechanism — aim, distance, strafe,
crits — simply never gets called.

⛔ NEXT TASK (core, not a patch): the "fight or flee" decision in `MobDefenseChain`. Fleeing
should be the EXCEPTION (low health, a crowd, a primed creeper), not the default answer to a

WHAT'S ALREADY READY FOR THAT MOMENT: the hookup itself, the `kaTung=tung/task/canHit/equip`

### G-1.121 — ⭐ CAUSE OF THE FLEEING FOUND: weapon damage on 1.21.11 was HARDCODED TO ZERO

Read `MobDefenseChain` in full, not from memory, and found the mechanism:

    //#if MC < 12111
    float damage = bestSword == null ? 0 : (bestSword.getMaterial().getAttackDamage()) + 1;
    //#else
    //$$ float damage = 0; // TODO [1.21.11] get attack damage from Item.Settings component
    //#endif

On 1.21.11 the old API was removed, leaving a STUB RETURNING ZERO. Further down:

    canDealWith = ceil(armor*3.6/20 + damage*0.8 + shield)

Without armor that's ceil(0) = 0, and the danger of one zombie is 1, so `canDealWith >= danger`
NEVER held — and the chain always fell into `else`: `RunAwayFromHostilesTask`, priority 80.
Hence "the bot with an iron sword and full health flees from a single zombie", and hence the
entire tungsten dueling mechanic was NEVER called even once.

FIX (core, no more branching): damage is now read from the item itself, from the attribute
modifier component, IDENTICALLY for 1.21.1 and 1.21.11. The attribute is looked up by registry
PATH (`attack_damage`), not by a constant — it's named differently across the two versions, but
the meaning of the question is the same.

MEASURED (night, mob spawning off, one zombie, iron sword):
- BEFORE: `mdRet7` (flee), zombie stayed at 20.0 HP the whole session, `mdTung=0`;
- AFTER: `mdRet6=57` (decided to fight), `mdTung=57..124`, no flight (`mdRet3`=`mdRet7`=0).

⛔ NOT FINISHED. The strike still doesn't land:
1. movement was shared by TWO owners (the task was walking toward the target, the controller was
   holding distance) — separated by distance: approach belongs to the task, striking to
   tungsten. After this `dteInRange` grew from 0 -> 126;
2. but the zombie is still at 20.0 HP. Strike gates: `total=161 click=0 cd=59 reach=98 angle=63
   los=0 passed=8` — eight strikes PASSED, yet no damage; and the counters FREEZE, i.e. the
   controller stops ticking. Next pass: why does `passed=8` deal no damage (wrong target on the
   controller's side? the strike failing a server-side distance check?) and why does the tick
   stop.

### G-1.128 — ⭐ POSITION FREEZE CLOSED: rewinding FORWARD wasn't resetting movements

MECHANISM (found by reading `MovementQueue` in full, not from memory). `snap()` has two
branches:
- BACKWARD — resets movements (`reset()`), and the same file records WHY: the SUCCESS status is
  "sticky", `updateState` returns control immediately if the status isn't RUNNING/PREPPING, so
  replaying an already-finished movement REPORTS SUCCESS while doing nothing. Without the reset
  this once produced `mqSteps=14365` on a 14-step chain;
- FORWARD — used to land on `i - 1` WITHOUT a reset. The same defect from the other side: we
  land on a movement that's already finished, it completes instantly, `index++`, we land again —
  and the chain gets BURNED THROUGH, steps pile up, the bot stands still.

This matches the measurement: 114 steps in a single poll with ONE chain start and a stationary
position, while backward rewinds for the whole run were only 16 — sixteen rewinds can't burn
through 114 steps, but a forward landing with no reset can.

FIX: a forward rewind now resets movements from the new index to the found one — symmetric with
the backward branch. Plus a `qBurn` counter ("steps completed without leaving the cell where the
chain started") — so "is the chain burning through" becomes a number, not a guess.

MEASUREMENT ON THE TARGET COURSE: `gamer_smoke 8 --repeat 3 --rung wood` -> **3/3 PASS, ZERO
freezes across the whole measurement, zero deaths, `qBurn=0`**. Before the fix, the same build
gave 2/3, specifically because of freezing.

BASELINE SUITES: `mob_melee` PASS (`mdTung total=64`, zombie dead, `min_hp=17`);
`nav` 11/12 on a HEALTHY host (`invalid: 0`), the failed `nav_bridge` green in ISOLATION —
goal reached in 10.8s, 0 falls, 0 freezes. So the failure in the suite doesn't reproduce in an
isolated run; a regression from the fix is not confirmed.

### G-1.129 — ⭐ DEATH NO LONGER CANCELS THE GOAL: `nav_bridge` GREEN, gate failures 0

MECHANISM (found by reading, confirmed by reproduction). `SingleTaskChain.onTick` finishes a
task on the condition `isFinished() || stopped()`, and the SECOND half fires when a task gets
INTERRUPTED — death with respawn is an ordinary case. `UserTaskChain.onTaskFinish` treats this as
completed work: it SHUTS DOWN the executor entirely, and the bot stands still after respawning
for the rest of the run.

Evidence from the failed `nav_bridge`'s artifact (timeline): t=4.8 the bot is bridging at x=17.1,
t=8.3 it's at **y=-193** (the void), t=12 it respawns at 0.5,-60,0.5 — and doesn't move for the
next FORTY SECONDS. A screenshot of the same run: `<no chain running>`. State after death, read
directly:

    active=false | (no chain running) | UserTaskChain(on=false)

meaning the executor was SHUT DOWN, not that the goal was achieved.

FIX: an interrupted (rather than completed) goal is now RESUMED — `mainTask.reset()` instead of
shutting down, up to 3 attempts (enough for a death + MLG + mob defense in a single run, while a
task that keeps stopping itself every tick will still eventually finish).

VERIFIED WITH A DIRECT EXPERIMENT (reproducible): goal x=90, killing the bot at x=36.6.
- BEFORE the fix: 32 seconds spent respawning, `mqStarted=0`, `active=false` — the bot is dead as
  far as the task is concerned;
- AFTER: `active=true`, the bot keeps going 28.3 -> 62.5 -> **90.6 (goal reached)**.

MEASUREMENTS: `nav` 11/12, **gate failures: 0**, `nav_bridge` PASS (was FAIL); the only non-PASS
is `nav_slime` INVALID from host starvation (9.9 fps against a 12 threshold) — a machine issue.
`mob_melee` PASS (`mdTung total=59`).

Along the way, in this same pass (also core): a position jump not explained by walking (death,
teleport, portal) now INVALIDATES the route in the move queue — it drops the chain and requests
replanning. Counter `qTp`. It didn't fire in this experiment because the queue never started at
all after death (`mqStarted=0`) — the guard is needed for cases where the queue is alive.

### G-1.130 — a guard on "planning", but it's NOT what's holding the remaining freezes

OLD EVIDENCE (stall_run2 from the previous measurement): `pdEnter=7478`, `pdWalking=0`,
`pdNear=26`, `dbTick=7521`, `rayMiss=7072`, `dbFar=29` with `dbDistSum=246` (an average of 8.5
blocks to the target). So the bot stood still for 90 seconds eight blocks from the needed block,
asked to approach 29 times — and didn't move, because the driver's final branch was returning
"I'm driving" while driving nothing: it holds the tick and blocks the fallback.

FIX: the branch is named (`pdPlan=plans/yields`) and LIMITED — if planning happens for 8 seconds
straight, the move queue never started, and the body hasn't moved a single block, the driver
yields the tick (`return false`), and the fallback gets the right to act. Eight seconds is
comfortably more than a healthy plan (it becomes a chain within a couple of ticks) and
comfortably less than the ninety seconds the bench counts as a freeze.

⛔ THE MEASUREMENT SAYS: THIS ISN'T IT. `gamer_smoke --repeat 3 --rung wood` -> 2/3 (threshold
2), zero deaths in all three, but **`pdPlan=4/0`** — the branch was taken only 4 times per run,
zero yields. So the guard is correct, but barely engaged in these runs, and SOMETHING ELSE is
holding the freezes.

NEW EVIDENCE (a fresh freeze snapshot): `pdEnter=118`, `pdPlan=0/0`, `pdNear=0`, `mqStarted=4`,
`dbTick=210`, `qTp=1`. The driver almost NEVER ENTERS (118 against 7478 previously), meaning this
time the freeze is held entirely outside the driver. A freeze is a FAMILY of symptoms with
different mechanisms, not one bug; each snapshot needs its own analysis.

NEXT PASS: analyze the `pdEnter=118` snapshot — who owns the tick when the driver never enters.

### G-1.131 — ⭐ A CLOCK THAT REWINDING CANNOT ERASE: a step can finally time out

FULL EVIDENCE (stall_run3, read IN FULL, not in pieces):

    mqStarted=91  mqSteps=1301  mqBack=87  mqTicks=5442  step=6/10  mqTimeout=0
    mvSteered=4810  moveTicks=5352  sprint=101/5352
    position unchanged for 90 seconds

Keys were being PRESSED almost every tick (4810 steering calls out of ~5440), the body wasn't
moving — and yet **not a single step timed out**. The cause is right there: 87 backward rewinds
for 91 chains. A rewind resets movements (correct — otherwise "sticky" SUCCESS), but the reset
zeroes `ticksOnCurrent`, i.e. THE STEP'S CLOCK. The loop: stuck -> drift-triggered rewind -> reset
-> stuck, and the timeout NEVER accumulates.

FIX (core): the clock now lives on the QUEUE, not on the movement, and measures the BODY: if the
body hasn't left its cell for 120 ticks (6 seconds) while actively being steered, the chain is
dropped and a replan is requested. A rewind cannot erase it, because the clock is about the
queue, not the movement.

MEASUREMENT: `gamer_smoke 8 --repeat 3 --rung wood` -> 2/3 (threshold 2), zero deaths, and
**`qNoMove=1` — the guard FIRED**. This sets it apart from the two previous guards (`pdPlan=4/0`,
`slotYeet=0`), which never fired once: the mechanism was correctly identified.

⛔ HONESTLY: the score didn't move (2/3 both before and after), two freezes over the measurement.
So the mechanism is closed, but it WASN'T THE ONLY ONE — the family remains. Next pass: take a
fresh snapshot with THIS guard already in place and see which signature is left.

### G-1.132 — MANUAL GRID CRAFTING (user requirement) + an honest regression 2/3 -> 1/3

DONE: `useCraftingBookToCraft` is now **false by default** — crafting proceeds by placing items

⛔ HONEST MEASUREMENT RESULT: `gamer_smoke 8 --repeat 3 --rung wood` -> **1/3 (was 2/3)**,
4 freezes. One run went through the ladder well and WITHOUT THE BOOK: first craft 22.2s -> wood

CONCLUSION: the manual path works, but it's LESS WELL DEBUGGED than the book path, and it's now

### G-1.133 — ⭐ 3/3: materials were getting stuck IN THE CRAFTING GRID ITSELF, and the check couldn't see them

THE REGRESSION FROM G-1.132 (manual crafting: 2/3 -> 1/3) IS CLOSED. Mechanism found by reading
the snapshot in full:

    ciTick=8051  ciCollect=8051  ciReceive=0   shIssued=1008   cgScreen=class_1723
    task: <Doing stuff in crafting_table container> -> <Collect Recipe Resources> Getting stick x2

`ciCollect` EQUALS `ciTick` — meaning EVERY tick the bot decided there were no materials and went
off to collect them. Cause: `hasRecipeMaterialsOrTarget` looks IN THE INVENTORY, while manual
crafting (now the default) puts ingredients IN THE GRID. Any interruption leaves them there — and
the bot stands at the workbench, "collecting sticks", while its planks sit in the grid right in
front of it.
