### G-1.134 — ⭐ "STANDS AT THE EDGE" WAS AN FPS DEPENDENCY. FIXED.

USER COMPLAINT (2026-08-05, from a video): "it approaches the edge of the platform AND STANDS
THERE, doing jack — is that supposed to be normal? it's supposed to work rock solid."

DIAGNOSIS. Same course, same build, different result:
    16.3 fps -> goal in 11.0s, PASS
     9.9 fps (while recording) -> stands at the edge, 11.6 blocks from the goal, 16 freeze windows
Cause: `WindMouseRotation.applyRenderStep` moves the aim by a FIXED step PER FRAME, while the
world, mobs and block placement run at 20 ticks per second. At 10 fps the head turns TWICE as
slow — and anything requiring the crosshair to be aimed before acting (a block face for
bridging) starves exactly when the host is under load.

FIX (core): the aim step is now a speed OVER TIME, rather than per frame. A frame that lasted
twice as long gets twice the rotation; clamped at a floor of 1.0 (at >= 20 fps the behavior does
NOT change at all — the fix only gives back what a dropped frame took away), capped at 4x on
top so a lag spike doesn't turn into a teleport.

MEASURED UNDER THE SAME CONDITIONS WHERE THE EMBARRASSMENT HAPPENED (while recording): **PASS,
goal in 11.2s, 0 falls, 0 freezes** (was: standing at the edge).
BASELINES: `nav` **12/12, 0 gate failures**; `mob_melee` PASS.

CONCLUSION 3: **the default of 2.4 is the minimum on both measures**. Distance tuning is

game itself checks, so flowing lava/water are counted correctly). `MovementHelper` import:

### #29 — the "duplicate placement planners" item is NOT A DELETION, IT'S A CONSOLIDATION (verified)

The item was phrased as "delete the duplicate", and I went to close it out. Checking the code
says otherwise: BOTH planners are ALIVE.
- `FastPlanner` (path/fast) — the block A* that currently drives the bot;
- `BlockSpacePathFinder` (path/blockSpaceSearchAssist) — called FROM THE MIXIN
  (`MixinClientPlayerEntity:196`) and from `PathFinder:959,963`.
Both read the same `planPlaceMoves` flag, but they're different implementations, not a copy.

### G-0 — why `BaritoneAPI` can't be removed "piecemeal" (verified)
The five usages aren't imports, they're a REAL tie to the engine: the central accessor
`getClientBaritone()` (AltoClef:845), two `BlockStateInterface`s (PreEquipItemChain, WorldHelper),
an event handler in the mixin, and a setting value in a custom goal. Removing any one of them

transition, not a standalone unit. The first real G-0 unit (MovementHelper -> vanilla checks) is

### G-2.1 — PASS 15: FOUND A CRIT-JUMP TIMING BUG (crit share x2), but damage taken DID NOT drop

STARTING MEASUREMENT: over a fight with the trio the bot lands **1 crit per 13 hits (7.7%)** —
while the whole point of jumping in combat is exactly the crits. A crit only counts on landing.

BUG IN THE CODE (its own comment claims the opposite): takeoff was allowed at a strike charge of
0.55-0.92. The jump takes ~6 ticks, while the full cooldown at base attack speed is 12.5 ticks;
so from 0.55 to the hit there remain ~5 ticks, and the bot strikes WHILE STILL RISING. From
(1 - cd) * 12.5 > 6 it follows that cd < 0.52 — the takeoff window is fixed to **0.25-0.50**.

MEASUREMENT: crit share **7.7% -> 16.7%** (3 crits out of 18 hits) — the mechanic works now.
BUT damage taken: 15 / 3 / 15 against 8.0 for circling — DID NOT improve (within noise, if
anything worse).

DECISION: KEEPING the fix — it corrects a real mismatch between the code and its own stated
intent and measurably doubles crits (i.e. outgoing damage), and "didn't improve incoming damage"
is a fact, not a reason to bring back broken timing. Suites after it: `nav` 12/12 (0 gate
failures), `mob_melee` PASS.

### G-2.1 — PASS 16: finishing off the most wounded target — WORSE (16th hypothesis, 14th rollback)

HYPOTHESIS 16 (per the "damage ~ contact time" law): right now the target is chosen by PROXIMITY
and changes every tick, so damage is spread thin — you can bring all three down to 1 HP and still
have all THREE hitting. A kill removes an attacker, so the most wounded one should be finished
off.

MEASUREMENT: 9 / 12 / 17 -> average 12.7 against 8.0. WORSE. ROLLED BACK (a comment with the
numbers added to the code so the idea doesn't resurface).
CAUSE: the bot starts RUNNING between targets instead of hitting the one in front of it — and
this, again, lengthens the fight.

## TALLY OF G-2.1 AFTER 16 PASSES: 2 LOCKED IN, 14 ROLLED BACK. CRITERION NOT MET.
Locked in: circling without random flip-flopping (15.3 -> 8.0) and crit-jump timing (crits
7.7% -> 16.7%). Ideas WITHIN the test's conditions are EXHAUSTED. The remaining two options
change the conditions and await the user's decision: ARMOR (not in the loadout; physically cuts
damage, but that's gear, not skill) and a SHIELD held continuously instead of trading blows.

### G-2.2 — ⭐ THE SKELETON COURSE WAS INVALID: the bot never fought at all. FIXED, baseline taken.

THE VERY FIRST MEASUREMENT (3 runs) showed a complete failure on every criterion: the skeleton
ALWAYS survives, `mdTung=0`, the bot drops to 1-3 HP. A live sample during the fight: **ALL**
`mdRet` slots at zero — the defense chain never ticked at all while the bot was being shot
(16 -> 7 -> 4 HP).

THE CAUSE IS IN MY COURSE, NOT THE BOT. The `@test kill` command in `Playground` looks ONLY for
zombies (`ZombieEntity`). The arena had a skeleton -> the task is never created -> the executor
idles -> and with no active task the defense chain doesn't tick (I'd measured this before). The
bot was simply standing there.

FIXED IN TWO STEPS, each based on fact, not a guess:
1. added an `@test killhostile` command — takes the nearest hostile, not just a zombie;
2. it first printed "No hostiles found", because `getTrackedEntities` indexes by a SPECIFIC
   class and answers nothing for `HostileEntity`. Used the ready-made
   `getEntityTracker().getHostiles()` list — the same one the defense chain itself uses.

BASELINE AFTER THE FIX (3 runs): **skeleton dead in all three**, the fight goes through tungsten
(`mdTung` 61 / 102 / 68), but the damage criterion is NOT met: `min_hp` 4 / 9 / 7, meaning
several arrows land instead of the one allowed.

NEXT STEP FOR G-2.2 (exactly what the user asked for): computing the trajectory of THE ENEMY'S
arrow and stepping off the line BEFORE the shot. Right now the bot just walks up to the skeleton
and takes the volleys. tungsten has `TrajectorySolver` (for OUR shooting) and `SafetySystem` — an
inverse calculation is needed: enemy projectile -> entry point into our hitbox -> shift
perpendicular to the line of fire.

### G-2.2 — arrow dodging DID NOT WORK (rolled back), and priority was reassigned by the user

Wrote the calculation: a flying arrow is an entity with a velocity, so the intersection of its
line with our hitbox and the time to impact are plain arithmetic; on a predicted hit — step
PERPENDICULAR to the line. First placed the check inside `closeQuarters` — it never got called
(overridden by the safety arbiter and lack of line of sight). Moved it above the arbiter. Live
measurement DURING a fight: `arrowDodge=0` and `mdTung=0/0` — still never fires. The `min_hp`
improvement (12/13/12 against 4/8/2) seen after moving it has NOTHING to do with the fix: it's
spread. ROLLED BACK.
